# Syntyr CSS — consolidated public reference

Source-tree version: 0.3.0-alpha.5 (may be an unreleased candidate).
Published immutable release: 0.3.0-alpha.4.

WARNING: This reference follows repository source. Before generating markup,
check the installed release and CSS modules. Do not assume alpha.5 features
exist in the published alpha.4 release. Syntyr is CSS, not a JS widget library.

Generated from an explicit allowlist by scripts/build_agent_docs.py.
Do not edit this file directly.
Relative links below are relative to each original source file, not this combined file.

## Source: docs/getting-started.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/getting-started.md

# Getting started with Syntyr CSS

Build a useful page with **one stylesheet and semantic HTML**. Syntyr ships
plain CSS: no Node.js, JavaScript runtime, provider, build plugin, or package
manager is required in your application.

> **Release boundary (November 2026):** The latest published release is
> [v0.3.0-alpha.4](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/releases/tag/v0.3.0-alpha.4).
> The repository's 0.3.0-alpha.5 source is an **unreleased candidate**.
> The CSS examples below work with published alpha.4; the optional static
> HTML checker described later is packaged only in the proposed alpha.5 ZIP.

## 1. Copy the released CSS

Download the **published alpha.4 ZIP**, extract it, and copy
`dist/syntyr.core.css` into your site's public CSS directory, for example
`public/css/syntyr.core.css`. The file is ready to use as-is.

For a quick preview, you can use the
[immutable version-pinned CDN asset](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css).
For production, self-hosting the pinned asset avoids an extra network origin.

## 2. Paste a complete working page

Save this as `index.html` in a site that serves the copied stylesheet at
`/css/syntyr.core.css`:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My first Syntyr page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
</head>
<body class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <main class="syn-shell" id="main">
    <article class="syn-panel">
      <h1 class="syn-heading">Project overview</h1>
      <p>A page built with HTML and one CSS file.</p>
      <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/projects">
        View projects
      </a>
    </article>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

Serve the directory with your existing application server. If you open this
HTML directly as `file://`, replace the `/css/` URL with the actual
relative path to the stylesheet. Replace the example `/projects` link with
a real route in your application.

Use `syn-root` around the part of the page you want Syntyr to style.
Without that scope, component classes will not receive their Syntyr styles.
Change `data-syn-theme` to `grid` or `noir` to use either of the
other published alpha.4 themes.

## 3. Choose the *minimum* CSS you need

- **Default:** `syntyr.core.css` — tokens and explicit component classes.
- **Optional semantic HTML:** load `syntyr.semantic.css` **after** core;
  add `syn-semantic` to the scoped root to style ordinary HTML elements.
- **Optional SaaS layouts:** load `syntyr.recipes.css` after core when using
  documented recipes.
- **Optional decorative effects:** use `syntyr.effects.css` only if needed.

Do not combine `syntyr.all.css` with individual modules, or
`syntyr.css` with core and effects. These bundles overlap.

Read the [component reference](components.md), [recipe reference](recipes.md),
and [framework integrations](framework-integrations.md) for HTML variants
and host-application responsibilities. Syntyr styles controls; your app
provides form handling, data access, authorization, and navigation.

## 4. Validate markup (optional, alpha.5 ZIP candidate)

After the alpha.5 archive is released, its extracted root will include
`scripts/syntyr_check.py` and `metadata/syntyr-contract.json`.
The checker requires **Python 3.10+ on the developer machine only**;
it ships no JavaScript or build-time requirement to consumers.

From the **extracted matching-version archive**, check your HTML file:

```sh
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py /path/to/your/index.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --format json /path/to/your/index.html
```

It reports misspelled `syn-*` classes, invalid literal state values,
unscoped classes in complete documents, and missing optional CSS files when
it can identify the installed stylesheets. For HTML fragments with no links,
pass the actual modules using `--stylesheets syntyr.core.css`.
Dynamic template expressions are skipped, not executed.

**Do not run the candidate checker against published alpha.4 CSS** and assume
its alpha.5 class inventory is accurate for alpha.4. Use matching-version
metadata; this is a static HTML check, not an accessibility or runtime audit.
See the [editor and validator guide](editor-integration.md).

## 5. Optional package-manager projects

`@syntyr/css` is prepared in the alpha.5 source, but it is **not yet published to npm**.
Do not assume `npm install @syntyr/css` works today. If your application
already uses a bundler, the source candidate supports a locally packed
tarball; follow the [package-manager guide](package-managers.md).
Applications that don't use a build tool can remain on copied CSS indefinitely.

## Check before production

Test real routes and submission behavior, keyboard focus, zoom/reflow,
forced colors, and browser compatibility in your own application. Alpha
releases are experimental and do not carry a v1 compatibility or accessibility
conformance guarantee. [Release guidance](distribution.md) and
[accessibility checklist](accessibility.md) explain the current boundaries.

## Source: docs/ai-quickstart.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/ai-quickstart.md

# Syntyr CSS: AI-agent quickstart

Use this guide when creating an application **with** Syntyr. To modify Syntyr itself, also read the repository [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/AGENTS.md). Syntyr supplies styles, **not** application logic or a JavaScript component system.

## 1. Choose the correct version

| Version | Status | Themes | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0.3.0-alpha.4` | Published immutable release | `grid`, `noir`, `studio` | Safe to pin for examples below |
| `0.3.0-alpha.5` | Unreleased source candidate | Seven themes including `industrial`, `terminal`, `corporate`, `minimal` | Do not cite as a downloadable tagged release |

For a production application, copy a tagged CSS release to your own origin and pin its version. The CDN URL below is suitable for an initial prototype:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css">
```

For page-level recipes, load the same **version** of the optional module after core:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.recipes.css">
```

Do not combine `syntyr.all.css` with individual CSS modules; that loads duplicates. A stylesheet is not automatically installed by adding a `syn-*` class to markup.

### One-file semantic HTML (unreleased source only)

If testing alpha.5 from a local source checkout, `syntyr.semantic-bundle.css` includes both core and optional semantic rules. Do **not** point a production page at a nonexistent alpha.5 CDN release URL.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.semantic-bundle.css">
<main class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <article><h1>Settings</h1><button type="button">Save</button></article>
</main>
```

Use `.syn-root` and `.syn-semantic` together; the bundle does not globally restyle arbitrary host HTML. Never load it alongside `core.css` or `semantic.css`, which would duplicate CSS. [Complete source demo](../examples/semantic-starter.html).

## 2. Generate valid HTML

```html
<main class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-shell">
    <header class="syn-header">
      <a href="/" class="syn-logo">Acme</a>
      <nav aria-label="Primary navigation"><a href="/reports">Reports</a></nav>
    </header>
    <section class="syn-panel" aria-labelledby="reports-title">
      <h1 class="syn-heading" id="reports-title">Reports</h1>
      <p class="syn-muted">View recent activity.</p>
      <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/reports/new">New report</a>
    </section>
  </div>
</main>
```

All classes in this sample are available from published alpha.4 core. Use an `<a>` for navigation, a `<button>` for an action, and functional `href`/`action` values rather than dummy `#` placeholders.

## 3. Use responsive recipes only when their module is loaded

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-region" data-syn-theme="studio" aria-label="Operations overview">
  <div class="syn-stats">
    <article class="syn-stat">
      <p class="syn-stat-label">Open tickets</p>
      <p class="syn-stat-value">14</p>
    </article>
    <article class="syn-stat">
      <p class="syn-stat-label">Resolved today</p>
      <p class="syn-stat-value">8</p>
    </article>
  </div>
</section>
```

`syn-region` and `syn-stats` are core classes; they use native container queries. The containing region must be an ancestor of the responsive pattern. For application shells, `syn-app-shell` is in **recipes**, not core.

## 4. Optional scoped semantic mode

Load `syntyr.semantic.css` **after core**, then opt into `syn-semantic` in a `syn-root` subtree. Ordinary HTML outside that subtree is unaffected.

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="noir">
  <form action="/login" method="post">
    <label for="email">Email <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required></label>
    <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
  </form>
</section>
```

The form must have a real server handler. Syntyr does not provide authentication, CSRF protection, requests or validation logic.

## 5. Framework rules and accessibility

- **React/JSX:** use `className`, `htmlFor`, and normal framework event handlers. Syntyr styles HTML but does not expose React components.
- **HTMX/Datastar:** let the host library manage state and requests; preserve native form behavior. For transient class-changing elements inside semantic mode, see the [framework integration guide](framework-integrations.md) for `data-syn-semantic`.
- **Themes:** `data-syn-theme` belongs on `.syn-root` or a nested themed subtree. Prefer `studio` for professional SaaS, `grid`/`noir` for cinematic interfaces.
- **Accessibility:** preserve keyboard focus, form labels, descriptive error messages, link destinations and reduced-motion preferences. `aria-pressed` describes an actual pressed toggle; `aria-busy` alone does not perform loading.
- **Visualization:** `syntyr.viz.css` styles provided SVG and HTML. It **does not calculate chart geometry** or provide a renderer.
- **Custom theme:** override documented `--syn-*` variables in application CSS. Verify text/background and interactive contrast.

## 6. Verify generated output

1. Identify the installed Syntyr **version** and CSS modules.
2. Check every `syn-*` class against [components](components.md), [recipes](recipes.md), or the [validated curated manifest](../metadata/components.json).
3. Ensure the browser actually loads each required stylesheet, without duplicates.
4. Check interactive elements, keyboard navigation, high-zoom reflow and browser console.
5. Do not claim a static Syntyr example implements fetching, persistence, sorting, filtering or authentication.

See [agent integration](agent-integration.md) for reusable prompt instructions.

## Source: docs/design-principles.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/design-principles.md

# Design principles and conformance contract

Status: **unreleased alpha.5 source guidance**. Syntyr is a scoped, CSS-first
presentation system, not a JavaScript widget library. This guide distills
practices shared by mature design systems (Material, Fluent, Carbon, Spectrum,
Atlassian, Apple HIG and USWDS) into **portable rules** rather than borrowing
any brand's visual assets or platform-specific components.

**Priority order:** semantic meaning and accessibility > readable hierarchy and
feedback > predictable composition > optional aesthetics. When those conflict,
an ornamental effect or familiar-looking mockup must give way.

## Universal defaults

1. **Information hierarchy:** one clear page purpose, useful heading order,
   one primary action per decision area and subdued secondary actions. Use
   headings for structure, not to obtain a large font.
2. **Consistent spacing:** begin with `--syn-space-1` through
   `--syn-space-5`. Group related controls closely, separate different
   content regions deliberately. There is no universally correct 8px grid.
3. **Readable typography:** prefer `--syn-type-body`, `--syn-type-heading`,
   `--syn-type-section`, `--syn-type-display` and the shared body leading.
   Use legible text and avoid substituting tiny fonts for compact density.
4. **Semantic HTML and familiar behavior:** actions use buttons; navigation
   uses links; labeled inputs use native controls; tables have real headers.
   Prefer `details`, `dialog` and `popover` when their native behavior fits.
5. **Meaningful color roles:** use `--syn-bg`, `--syn-surface`, `--syn-text`,
   `--syn-muted`, `--syn-accent`, `--syn-on-accent`, and named
   success/warning/danger tokens. Color is never the only status cue.
6. **Accessible interaction:** visible `:focus-visible`, contrast, keyboard
   reachability, target size, label/description associations, readable error
   text, narrow-screen reflow, 200%/400% zoom and reduced motion.
   Target WCAG 2.2 AA in representative, *rendered* application flows.
7. **Responsive context:** adapt layouts to available space; prefer intrinsic
   layout and container queries for embedded regions. Never let dense tables
   silently clip important data; make overflow regions keyboard reachable.
8. **Feedback and recovery:** every mutation needs truthful pending, success
   and error feedback from its host application; invalid fields should explain
   correction and preserve input. CSS does not implement validation or alerts.
9. **Progressive disclosure:** defer uncommon settings inside clearly named
   native disclosures or separate screens. Do not hide essential actions.
10. **Independent customization:** theme, density, geometry, typography and
    intensity are separate axes. Customizations change semantic tokens; avoid
    per-theme component forks and `!important` escalation.

These are implementation principles, not proof that a particular page satisfies
accessibility law. See [DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md), [architecture](../ARCHITECTURE.md)
and [the accessibility guide](accessibility.md).

## Component state contract

| Component family | Real semantics | Required presentation and verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Action buttons | `button type="button"` or `button type="submit"`; `a href` only for navigation | default, hover when meaningful, `:focus-visible`, pressed, true disabled; distinguish toggle `aria-pressed` from decoration |
| Inputs and form groups | paired `label` + `id`, `fieldset`/`legend`, optional `aria-describedby` | default, focus, disabled, `:user-invalid` or synchronized `aria-invalid`, explicit error text |
| Navigation | `nav`, real links, `aria-current` on current destination | visible keyboard focus, active destination, wrapping/overflow, short discernible names |
| Data tables | `caption`, `th scope`, numeric cells when helpful | row/cell hierarchy, legible density, focusable overflow region, optional `aria-sort` only when sorting exists |
| Native overlays | `details`/`summary`, `dialog`, or `popover` | open/closed, visible focus, Escape/dismissal according to browser API; host owns custom focus logic |
| Feedback and status | meaningful text, optionally `role="status"`/`role="alert"` | not color-only; convey busy, success, warning and errors truthfully |
| Loading | host-owned lifecycle and message; optional decorative `.syn-skeleton` | never use skeletons as the only status announcement; `aria-busy` does not disable a button |
| Panels and layouts | `main`, `section`, headings, labels | stable reading order, logical spacing, mobile reflow and no accidental nesting of landmarks |

A state that exists only visually is not a substitute for a corresponding native
or accessible semantic state. Avoid fabricating `aria-selected`, `aria-busy`
or `aria-disabled` to make a screenshot resemble a working application.
See [components](components.md), [component authoring](component-authoring.md)
and [form composition recipes](component-recipes.md).

## Composition examples

The following copy-owned patterns use **only `syntyr.core.css`**. The
backend/application is responsible for actual operations, authorization,
pending-state announcements, validation and persistence. Paths and records
are illustrative, not implemented service endpoints.

### 1. Responsive overview with sensible emphasis

```html
<main class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="studio"
      data-syn-density="comfortable">
  <header>
    <h1>Campaign overview</h1>
    <p class="syn-muted">Review active campaigns and recent changes.</p>
    <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/campaigns/new">New campaign</a>
  </header>
  <section class="syn-region" aria-labelledby="overview-heading">
    <h2 id="overview-heading">Current activity</h2>
    <div class="syn-stats">
      <article class="syn-stat">
        <h3 class="syn-stat-label">Active campaigns</h3>
        <p class="syn-stat-value">12</p>
      </article>
      <article class="syn-stat">
        <h3 class="syn-stat-label">Pending reviews</h3>
        <p class="syn-stat-value">3</p>
      </article>
    </div>
  </section>
</main>
```

Use `.syn-region` *outside* the responsive `.syn-stats` children so the
container query measures the available panel width, not the viewport.
Display real values from the application rather than assuming CSS can compute
metrics.

### 2. Native GET filter and accessible data table

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" aria-labelledby="records-title">
  <h2 id="records-title">Accounts</h2>
  <form class="syn-form" method="get" action="/accounts">
    <label class="syn-label" for="account-query">Account name</label>
    <input class="syn-input" id="account-query" type="search" name="q">
    <div class="syn-actions">
      <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">Filter accounts</button>
      <a class="syn-button" href="/accounts">Clear filter</a>
    </div>
  </form>
  <div class="syn-table-wrap" role="region" aria-label="Accounts table"
       tabindex="0">
    <table class="syn-table">
      <caption>Account directory</caption>
      <thead>
        <tr><th scope="col">Account</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><th scope="row">Northwind</th><td>Active</td></tr>
        <tr><th scope="row">Contoso</th><td>Review needed</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

Avoid `role="grid"` unless the application implements grid keyboard
interaction. If the backend filters the table, preserve the user's query and
announce updated results appropriately. These CSS classes style the native
elements but never sort, search or persist data.

### 3. Labeled settings with progressive disclosure

```html
<main class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <h1>Organization settings</h1>
  <form class="syn-form" action="/settings" method="post">
    <fieldset class="syn-fieldset">
      <legend>Organization details</legend>
      <div class="syn-field">
        <label class="syn-label" for="org-name">Name</label>
        <input class="syn-input" id="org-name" name="name" required
               aria-describedby="org-hint">
        <p class="syn-help" id="org-hint">Shown to your teammates.</p>
      </div>
      <details class="syn-details">
        <summary>Advanced settings</summary>
        <label class="syn-label" for="timezone">Time zone</label>
        <select class="syn-select" id="timezone" name="timezone">
          <option value="UTC">UTC</option>
          <option value="America/Sao_Paulo">Brasília</option>
        </select>
      </details>
    </fieldset>
    <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">
      Save settings
    </button>
  </form>
</main>
```

A real POST handler must check CSRF, permissions and validity. On an error,
rerender entered values, set `aria-invalid="true"` for invalid fields,
associate the actual error text via `aria-describedby`, and provide a
perceivable status. The demo deliberately does not fake saved-state feedback.

For richer CRM, filter toolbar and enterprise layout compositions, reuse
[existing recipes](recipes.md), [data-table guidance](data-tables.md)
and [the static CRM example](../examples/crm.html). Do not create redundant
CSS classes solely to implement these HTML patterns.

## Deliberate non-defaults

**Never universalize** Material-style elevation, glass effects, a specific
border radius, an 8px-only grid, desktop-like density, animation, or a single
navigation pattern. These are product/platform choices. Studio's quiet neutral
presentation is the default; Grid, Noir, strong effects, geometry and
additional density are opt-in. Style must never reduce semantic or accessibility
quality. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and `forced-colors`.

## Automated check and review protocol

Run the source-level semantic palette check:

```sh
python3 scripts/design_conformance.py
python3 scripts/design_conformance.py --format json
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_design_conformance.py'
```

It evaluates **12 defined semantic foreground/background roles across seven
built-in palettes (84 pair checks)** and fails closed for missing or
nonliteral colors. Roles are explicit so design changes cannot silently skip a
required pairing. This checks static source colors, including the primary
button foreground, link/accent, statuses, visible focus/accent against surfaces,
and strong borders. It is included in the standard Python test suite.

## What automated checks do not prove

The tool **does not validate rendered contrast** involving gradients,
`color-mix()`, overlays, icon graphics, every hover/focus interaction,
user-defined palettes, `light-dark()` computed values, nested theme paint
compositing or transparent surfaces. Nor does it validate keyboard behavior,
screen-reader announcements, zoom/resize, actual touch targets, server errors,
or brand/legal accessibility certification.

For release approval, separately run the browser/reflow/axe matrices and
record genuine keyboard, screen-reader, 200%/400% browser zoom, real OS
high-contrast and manual color-contrast evidence. Inconclusive axe nodes stay
unresolved until checked on their *effective painted backgrounds*. See the
[alpha.5 review log](accessibility-alpha5-review.md). Do not claim WCAG
conformance from this palette report.

## Source: docs/components.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/components.md

# Syntyr CSS component and token contract

Status: **experimental v0.3-alpha**, not yet released to a package registry. All CSS and markup are original to this repository; no upstream source code was copied.

Native elements such as `search`, `figure`, `figcaption`, `kbd`, `mark`, `output`, `meter`, and `pre` are styled only in the optional semantic mode. Native classless forms receive vertical spacing, fieldsets group controls, tables can use real `caption` elements, and disclosure summaries retain browser markers and comfortable pointer targets. See [the no-JS native example](../examples/native-elements.html). The regular component-class API and HTML outside `.syn-root` are unchanged.

## Loading and scoping

For the explicitly classed API (no automatic unclassed element styles):

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.core.css">
<body class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Run</button>
</body>
```

For Pico-like semantic markup, add the optional file **after** core and mark the subtree. Unclassed elements style automatically; opt in class-changing elements with `data-syn-semantic`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.semantic.css">
<section class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <article>
    <label for="id">Operator <input id="id" name="id" required></label>
    <button data-syn-semantic>Continue</button>
  </article>
</section>
```

Use `article` only for genuinely self-contained content; to draw a visual
card around a generic region use `.syn-panel` on the appropriate native
element. Use `fieldset` + `legend` to name control groups. In semantic mode
the default form layout applies to *unclassed* `form` (or explicit
`data-syn-semantic`), while `.syn-form` and application-owned classes retain
their separate styling contract. Use `label` rather than placeholders to name
inputs, and always give buttons a deliberate `type`.

Class-based components, recipes, effects, and geometry apply only to elements
inside a Syntyr root, including classes attached directly to the root itself.
A bare Syntyr class on an unrelated host element is deliberately ignored, so
framework-owned components and existing application CSS are not restyled.
The root boundary is enforced through modern native CSS nesting with
a zero-specificity selector rather than a global reset. Checkboxes and
radio controls using the explicit styling API retain a minimum 24 CSS px box;
the surrounding label should provide additional activation area.

For optional effects, load `syntyr.effects.css`. `syntyr.css` is the convenient core + effects entry point. `syntyr.all.css` combines everything (semantic styling still requires `.syn-semantic`). `syn-root` should wrap any themed subtree; nested `data-syn-theme` overrides color tokens. The separate `data-syn-intensity="quiet|standard|cinematic"` attribute controls decorative strength on a root or nested region. Load `syntyr.geometry.css` for a `.syn-frame` with one shape and optional `.syn-frame--accent`. See the [visual-intensity guide](visual-intensity.md).

## Components

| Area | CSS API | Semantic alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Buttons | `.syn-button`, `.syn-button--primary`, `.syn-button--outline`, `.syn-button--danger`, `.syn-button--small`, `.syn-button--ghost` | unclassed `button` |
| Panels | `.syn-panel`, `.syn-panel--cut` | unclassed `article` |
| Layout | `.syn-page` (viewport-height opt-in), `.syn-shell`, `.syn-header`, `.syn-grid`, `.syn-layout`, `.syn-inline`, `.syn-stack` | normal CSS layout |
| Typography | `.syn-logo`, `.syn-eyebrow`, `.syn-title`, `.syn-section-heading`, `.syn-heading`, `.syn-lede`, `.syn-mono`, `.syn-caption`, `.syn-muted` | native heading/text |
| Status | `.syn-badge`, `.syn-badge--accent`, `.syn-status` and semantic variants, `.syn-alert`, `.syn-alert--danger`, `.syn-meter` on `progress` | native `progress` |
| Forms | `.syn-form`, `.syn-label`, `.syn-input`, `.syn-select`, `.syn-textarea`, `.syn-check`, `.syn-fieldset`, `.syn-help`, `.syn-error` | unclassed form controls |
| Form compositions | `.syn-field`, `.syn-field-row`, `.syn-field-body`, `.syn-input-group`, `.syn-input-addon` | native `form`, `label`, `input`, `button` |
| Overlays | `.syn-popover` on `[popover]`, `.syn-dialog` on `dialog`, `.syn-details` on `details` | browser defaults |
| Data | `.syn-table-wrap`, `.syn-table`, `.syn-cell--wrap`, `.syn-cell--nowrap`, `.syn-cell--numeric` | unclassed `table` |
| Navigation | `.syn-breadcrumbs`, `.syn-pagination`, `.syn-page-link` | native `<nav>`, `<ol>`, links and `aria-current` |
| Workflow (unreleased) | `.syn-steps`, `.syn-step`, `.syn-steps--vertical` | ordered `<ol>` and `aria-current="step"` |
| Loading | `.syn-skeleton`, `.syn-skeleton--short` | decorative placeholders; announce status separately |
| Effects (optional) | `.syn-grid-effect`, `.syn-glow`, `.syn-scanlines` | none |

### Optional composition utilities and component overrides

Load `syntyr.utilities.css` in addition to core to use finite helpers:
`syn-u-w-full`, `syn-u-max-reading`, `syn-u-overflow-auto`,
`syn-u-text-center`, `syn-u-min-w-0` and `syn-u-wrap`. These classes
work only inside `.syn-root` and do not require a class generator.
The existing flex/grid/spacing helpers are unchanged. Load the optional
module only when it is needed.

Customize individual components with custom properties rather than a new
set of modifiers:

```html
<article class="syn-panel"
         style="--syn-panel-padding:1.5rem; --syn-panel-radius:.75rem;
                --syn-panel-border-width:2px">
  <button class="syn-button"
          style="--syn-button-padding-inline:1.25rem;
                 --syn-button-border-width:2px">Open</button>
</article>
```

Defaults preserve the previous appearance: fluid panel padding, square
panel corners, and 1px borders; button inline padding defaults to 1rem.
When `.syn-panel--cut` sits on a tinted or nested surface, set
`--syn-panel-cut-fill` to the **background behind the panel** so its cut
corner does not show the page-level `--syn-bg` by mistake. The default
remains `var(--syn-bg)` for existing flat page layouts.
These values are local CSS custom properties, not compile-time settings.
Inspect `metadata/syntyr-api.json` for the machine-readable API index,
or use the [editor integration instructions](editor-integration.md).

Optional native browser integrations: `.syn-popover--anchored` for invoker-relative popovers, `.syn-textarea--autosize` for `field-sizing: content`, and (with the optional `syntyr.motion.css` stylesheet) `.syn-popover--transition` and `.syn-reading-progress`. See the [browser API guide](native-browser-apis.md) for compatibility and fallbacks.

Use native button `popovertarget="id"` to control a popover and `commandfor="id" command="show-modal"` to open a dialog in supporting browsers. This last native dialog invoker API has newer browser support; provide alternate ways to reach important content where needed. Do not build custom ARIA dialog/tab/combobox patterns unless they are tested and necessary.

For component-level package imports and optional native UI recipes, see
[native patterns](native-patterns.md).

## Neutral-first visual styling

The implicit `.syn-root` palette is Studio (light and sans-serif). Explicit `data-syn-theme="grid"` and `data-syn-theme="terminal"` retain technical monospace presentation; other themes remain opt-in. `.syn-panel` and `.syn-stage` are flat by default; add `syn-surface--accent` from the optional recipes CSS for emphasis, or the effects stylesheet for cinematic treatments. `.syn-badge` is a neutral label; use `.syn-status` with readable status text for meaningful state, or `.syn-badge--accent` to emphasize a badge.

Use `.syn-section-heading` between `.syn-heading` and `.syn-display`. Table content wraps by default for better readability in narrow regions, including long text. Apply `.syn-cell--nowrap` to identifiers or short labels that must stay on one line; `.syn-cell--numeric` also preserves no-wrap numeric alignment. `.syn-cell--wrap` remains available to limit a descriptive cell to 38ch. Keep genuinely wide tables inside `.syn-table-wrap` with an accessible caption; for keyboard scrolling where needed, make the wrapper focusable with `tabindex="0"`, an accessible label and a visible focus ring. Selected rows have a logical inline-start accent border in addition to their fill.

For large server-rendered tables, see the [enterprise tables guide](data-tables.html) and [static example](../examples/data-tables.html). Sorting and filtering remain application responsibilities.

## Native HTML elements (optional semantic mode)

Syntyr styles common HTML primitives within `.syn-root.syn-semantic` or a `.syn-semantic` subtree of `.syn-root`. Load `syntyr.semantic.css` **after** `syntyr.core.css`. Without the semantic stylesheet and scope, ordinary HTML remains untouched.

| Native elements | Included presentation |
| --- | --- |
| `ul`, `ol`, `menu`, `li`, `dl`, `dt`, `dd` | List spacing, preserved native markers, definition terms |
| `h5`, `h6`, `small`, `abbr[title]`, `address` | Heading depth, readable captions, abbreviations, contact text |
| `pre`, `code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `mark` | Scrollable code, keyboard hints, sample output, contrast-safe highlights |
| `figure`, `figcaption`, `img`, `video`, `audio` | Captions and width-constrained media; intrinsic image/video proportions |
| `table`, `caption`, `progress`, `meter`, `output` | Data captions and native browser indicators |
| `input[type=file]`, `input[type=color]` | Native chooser controls with theme-aware surfaces |
| `details`, `summary`, `dialog`, `[popover]` | Browser-owned disclosure, top-layer behavior and dismissal |

The selectors style **unclassed elements only**, or elements explicitly marked `data-syn-semantic`. A classed element is left to its own application styles by default; no global element reset is added. Syntyr does not emulate native dialog or popover activation, file inputs, meters or input validation.

For a copyable page covering the additions, see [native HTML element examples](../examples/native-elements.html). The `commandfor` / `command="show-modal"` dialog button is progressively enhanced, not a guarantee for browsers that lack HTML invoker commands.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.semantic.css">
<main class="syn-root syn-semantic">
  <dl><dt>Availability</dt><dd>12 active screens</dd></dl>
  <figure><img src="/assets/preview.svg" alt="Campaign preview">
    <figcaption>Proof-of-posting image</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <label for="fill">Capacity</label>
  <progress id="fill" value="12" max="20">12 of 20</progress>
</main>
```

## Additional common UI elements and semantic HTML

The optional `syntyr.semantic.css` now covers the presentation-relevant
`hgroup`, `time`, `data`, `cite`, `dfn`, `var`, `q`, `ins`, `del`,
`picture`, `iframe`, `canvas`, and `svg` elements, plus native
`select[multiple]` and `textarea` without a `rows` attribute.
These styles apply only to unclassed elements inside `.syn-semantic` or to
elements with `data-syn-semantic`. Existing semantics, quotes, change
markings, media aspect ratios, and browser controls remain intact.

Elements like `bdi`, `bdo`, `ruby`, `rt`, `rp`, `wbr`, `template`,
`slot`, `option`, and `datalist` deliberately use native browser behavior.
Structural landmarks, `script`, and metadata do not need cosmetic component
APIs. **Not every HTML element benefits from a CSS reset.**

The core CSS adds these intentionally small presentation compositions:

| CSS API | Use case | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.syn-avatar`, `--sm`, `--lg`, `.syn-avatar-stack` | User or organization identities | Image or initials; decorative stack labels need a separate accessible group label |
| `.syn-chip` | Filter/category labels | Static or native anchor/button; `data-syn-state="active"` only changes visuals |
| `.syn-nav-tabs` | Section navigation | Ordinary links with `aria-current="page"`; **not** JavaScript tabs or tabpanels |
| `.syn-list-group`, `.syn-list-row` | Settings, destinations, item lists | Native list semantics; rows may contain anchors; `aria-current="page"` for current destination |
| `.syn-button-group` | Adjacent actions | Flexbox composition of real links/buttons; no artificial event handling |
| `.syn-divider-label` | Labeled separator | Decorative rules before/after actual text |
| `.syn-alert--success`, `.syn-alert--warning` | Notices | Extend existing `.syn-alert`; always include readable status/warning text |

Try the [CSS-only common UI example](../examples/common-ui.html) and the
[existing native elements example](../examples/native-elements.html).

```html
<nav class="syn-nav-tabs" aria-label="Account sections">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="/settings" aria-current="page">Settings</a></li>
    <li><a href="/billing">Billing</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
<ul class="syn-list-group" aria-label="Team members">
  <li><span class="syn-list-row"><span class="syn-avatar" aria-hidden="true">JD</span>Jane Doe</span></li>
</ul>
<p class="syn-alert syn-alert--warning">Review changes before publishing.</p>
```

Choose `aria-current="page"` only for real navigation state; do not use
`role="tab"` without implementing the WAI-ARIA keyboard and panel behavior.
Use `role="status"` or `role="alert"` only for genuinely dynamic
announcements, not because a box has a particular color. More complex
interactions (autocomplete, rich text editor, sortable tables, custom menus,
toast lifecycles) belong to the host app, not a CSS runtime.

## Theme tokens

| Token | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--syn-bg`, `--syn-surface`, `--syn-surface-hi` | Background surfaces |
| `--syn-text`, `--syn-muted` | Foreground text |
| `--syn-accent`, `--syn-on-accent`, `--syn-accent-soft` | Accent and contrast |
| `--syn-frame`, `--syn-danger` | Borders and warning states |
| `--syn-font`, `--syn-mono` | System typography |
| `--syn-space-1` ... `--syn-space-5` | Spacing scale |
| `--syn-cut`, `--syn-radius`, `--syn-line`, `--syn-control-height` | Shape and layout |

Application CSS can override tokens:

```css
/* Unlayered CSS overrides the library's layered defaults. */
.my-surface { --syn-accent: #a9f890; }
```

## Optional charts and microvisualizations

Load `syntyr.viz.css` after core for seven-theme chart colors, figure/legend
styling, inline SVG sparklines, bar lists, status trackers and heatmap cells.
Syntyr only styles supplied HTML/SVG; it does not create chart geometry,
fetch data or require a renderer. Read [Syntyr Viz](viz.md) and open the
[static seven-theme gallery](../examples/viz.html).

## Accessibility and performance contracts

- Actual semantic HTML and associated labels; use `button` for actions and `a` for navigation.
- Visible `:focus-visible` outline; do not remove it with theme overrides.
- Contrast target: WCAG 2.2 AA for text; manually verify any customized tokens.
- Honor user preferences: `prefers-reduced-motion`, `forced-colors`; effects opt-in and static.
- Avoid relying on color alone for state; use labels or icons with text alternatives.
- Raw/gzip bundle sizes are reported by `python3 scripts/asset_report.py`, with no hard size ceilings; runtime JS: 0 bytes.
- Browser coverage: current Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. The included automated browser suite runs Chromium when installed and can be extended to other engines.
- Do not automatically treat the demo or contract tests as an accessibility certification: test screen readers, 200%/400% zoom, form errors, contrast, and actual products separately.

## Distribution behavior

The repository now includes an **optional CSS-only `package.json` for package-manager distribution**; there is still no Node runtime requirement, bundling dependency, or mandatory package manager. A standard Python 3 build script creates deterministic concatenated CSS and validates exact committed outputs (see [optional package-manager guide](package-managers.md)):

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Licensing and provenance

MIT; this version is original work, not a fork or copy of Pico CSS, Chota or Open Props. If future work ports code from an upstream library, preserve that project's copyright and MIT notices and document the relevant files in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.


## Embedded versus full-page usage

`syn-root` provides a bounded styling context. Add `syn-page` **only for full-page experiences**. This separation prevents an embedded themed widget from unexpectedly forcing a viewport-height section.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="noir">
  <div class="syn-panel">This can be embedded inside an existing application.</div>
</section>
```

For invalid form controls, associate error text through native labeling and `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` for server-provided errors. `syn-error` changes text color; do not rely on color alone to communicate invalid state.

```html
<label class="syn-label" for="email">Email</label>
<input class="syn-input" id="email" type="email" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="email-error">
<p class="syn-error" id="email-error">Enter a valid email address.</p>
```

## v0.3 compositional patterns (no build step)

The following are ordinary CSS classes in `syntyr.core.css`:

| Class | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.syn-region` | Named `syn-region` inline-size container for independent widget responsiveness |
| `.syn-split` | Stacked by default; two columns at container width >=43rem |
| `.syn-stats` | One/two/three columns at container widths <31rem, >=31rem, >=55rem |
| `.syn-stat`, `.syn-stat-label`, `.syn-stat-value` | Semantic telemetry card presentation |
| `.syn-empty` | Centered dashed-outline empty-state composition |
| `.syn-pricing`, `.syn-price-card` | One column until 43rem, then three equal columns |
| `.syn-price-card[data-syn-featured]` | Opt-in highlighted plan, purely visual, no ARIA claim |
| `.syn-price-value`, `.syn-feature-list` | Pricing typography and list styles |
| `.syn-toolbar` | Wrapping flex toolbar |

Attach `.syn-region` **on an ancestor** of the patterns. A region element isn't its own query container descendant; without a region ancestor the patterns remain readable one-column layouts. Nest separate regions for independently sized widgets. The `syn-region` name prevents unrelated page containers from changing their layouts.

Button state: `.syn-button[aria-pressed="true"]` is a pressed **toggle button**; `[data-syn-state="active"]` is decoration/host state; `[aria-busy="true"]` expresses in-progress updates but does not actually disable interactions. State changes and form handling are application responsibilities.

Additional inherited tokens: `--syn-ease`, `--syn-duration-fast`, `--syn-success`, `--syn-warning`. Extend themes with unlayered `.syn-root[data-syn-theme="custom"] { --syn-accent: ... }` CSS. Test contrast for your own values.

See [theme customization and token overrides](theme-customization.md), [MIT composition recipes](recipes.md) and [Tailwind architectural research](tailwind-research.md).

## Optional SaaS, business and CLI compositions (development branch)

Load `syntyr.core.css` first and `syntyr.recipes.css` second. The core remains separate from optional recipes; measure each bundle instead of enforcing a fixed byte cap.

| Context | Optional classes |
| --- | --- |
| SaaS | `.syn-app-shell`, `.syn-app-rail`, `.syn-app-nav`, `.syn-workspace`, `.syn-app-topbar`, `.syn-kpi-grid`, `.syn-app-card`, `.syn-activity-list` |
| CRM / vertical SaaS | `.syn-filter-bar`, `.syn-filter-field`, `.syn-filter-actions`, `.syn-pipeline`, `.syn-pipeline-lane`, `.syn-pipeline-list`, `.syn-pipeline-card`, `.syn-record-fields` |
| Business website | `.syn-site-hero`, `.syn-site-heading`, `.syn-feature-grid`, `.syn-feature-card`, `.syn-cta-band` |
| Browser terminal | `.syn-terminal`, `.syn-terminal-bar`, `.syn-terminal-body`, `.syn-terminal-line`, `.syn-terminal-prompt` |
| Surface design | `.syn-frame--precision`, `.syn-frame--industrial`, `.syn-frame--soft` |

Native disabled buttons cannot activate; aria-disabled does not block activation by itself. Host application code must suppress actions when ARIA-disabled and should preserve focus when appropriate. Syntyr does not disable click handlers via CSS.

Professional light mode: `data-syn-theme="studio"`. Colors and geometry are intentionally independent. Use `.syn-table-emphasis` for explicit cell highlighting instead of relying on last-column position; `.syn-status--success`, `--warning`, or `--danger` should always accompany readable status text.

Native terminal applications cannot render CSS. Use `terminal/palettes.json` as the portable color reference. See [usage and accessibility guidance](saas-cli-business.md). For bevel, notch, bracket, inset and circuit frame geometry, load the optional geometry stylesheet and follow [the frame guide](geometry-terminal.md). All new visual classes are optional and require no runtime JavaScript.


## Minimalist compositions (experimental)

`syntyr.recipes.css` also includes `.syn-sidebar` (two-column intrinsic
sidebar/content), `.syn-switcher` (all-or-nothing responsive card row),
fluid typography utilities `.syn-fluid-display` / `.syn-fluid-lede`,
and `.syn-reading`. These are not part of `syntyr.core.css`.
Classless checkbox and radio labels align their controls inline when
`syntyr.semantic.css` and `.syn-semantic` are enabled. See
[the recipe guide](recipes.md) and [live example](../examples/minimalist-patterns.html).

## Visual role examples

The optional [design-state example](../examples/design-states.html) exercises active, selected, disabled, and invalid presentation across nested light/dark themes. It contains no application state machine, backend operation, or runtime JavaScript.

## Progressive rendering extensions

System-aware `data-syn-theme="auto"` is built into core CSS. Use optional
`syntyr.print.css` for printable reports and the
[progressive-enhancement guide](progressive-enhancement.md) for fallbacks.

### Workflow steps (source candidate only)

Use the core CSS module with native ordered-list semantics. Wrap the list in a
`.syn-region` **ancestor** for a horizontal layout at wide *container* widths;
the narrow presentation is vertical. Use `.syn-steps--vertical` to keep a
vertical layout at every width.

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-region" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <h2>Workspace setup</h2>
  <ol class="syn-steps" role="list" aria-label="Workspace setup progress">
    <li class="syn-step" data-syn-state="complete">
      <span class="syn-step-label">Account created (complete)</span>
    </li>
    <li class="syn-step" aria-current="step">
      <span class="syn-step-label">Configure workspace (current step)</span>
    </li>
    <li class="syn-step"><span class="syn-step-label">Invite team (not started)</span></li>
  </ol>
</section>
```

Use `aria-current="step"` on exactly the current step. The application must
supply completed/error state text; `data-syn-state="complete|error"` is only a
presentation hook, not an ARIA state. Numbered circles and connectors are
decorative; the real ordered list and labels convey order and meaning. Preserve
`role="list"` for list semantics in Safari when CSS removes list markers.
Never use colors alone to communicate completion or failure. CSS cannot
implement step navigation, eligibility checks or server-side transitions.
Long step descriptions and translated text keep numbered markers aligned at the
block start so vertical connectors do not cross the marker or its numeral.

See [the zero-JavaScript example](../examples/workflow-steps.html). These classes
are not included in the published immutable alpha.4 release.

## Source: docs/data-grid.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/data-grid.md

# Data-grid presentation (opt-in, CSS-only)

Syntyr styles **the presentation of an existing data grid**. It does not implement
virtualization, sorting, query execution, clipboard parsing, selection, row editing,
focus navigation, or authorized persistence. Apps such as Adacavo own those behaviors.

## Installation

Load `dist/syntyr.core.css` for tokens and then `dist/syntyr.data-grid.css`.
For an application with its own theme tokens, the standalone grid CSS can be used
without loading Syntyr core, provided the required `--syn-*` color, radius, and
font tokens are mapped inside a `.syn-root` subtree.

This module is not included in `syntyr.core.css` or `syntyr.css`; it is opt-in.
The all-in-one demo bundle includes it. There is **no JavaScript** dependency.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" data-syn-density="compact">
  <div class="syn-data-grid" role="grid" aria-label="Inventory"
       aria-rowcount="2" aria-colcount="1">
    <div class="syn-data-grid__viewport" role="region" tabindex="0"
         aria-label="Scrollable inventory">
      <div class="syn-data-grid__header" role="rowgroup">
        <div role="row" aria-rowindex="1" class="syn-data-grid__header-row">
          <div class="syn-data-grid__columnheader" role="columnheader"
               style="width:14rem">Inventory face</div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div role="row" aria-rowindex="2" class="syn-data-grid__row"
           style="position:relative;height:2.5rem">
        <div role="gridcell" class="syn-data-grid__cell"
             style="width:14rem" tabindex="0" aria-readonly="true">
          <span class="syn-data-grid__cell-text">Face 102</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <footer class="syn-data-grid__footer">1 record</footer>
  </div>
</section>
```

## API and responsibilities

The host supplies these classes on the appropriate existing elements:
`syn-data-grid`, `syn-data-grid__viewport`, `syn-data-grid__header`,
`syn-data-grid__columnheader`, `syn-data-grid__row`, `syn-data-grid__cell`,
`syn-data-grid__cell--numeric`, `syn-data-grid__editor`,
`syn-data-grid__toolbar`, `syn-data-grid__status`,
`syn-data-grid__loading` and `syn-data-grid__footer`.

For ellipsis on long text, wrap cell text in a
`<span class="syn-data-grid__cell-text">`; ellipsis cannot reliably apply to
anonymous flex items. Keep the wrapper shrinkable. Editors and other interactive
controls remain application-owned and need their own layout/focus handling.

Nearest density scope wins: `compact`, `comfortable` (including resets), or
`spacious` on the grid itself or an ancestor. Match any virtualizer's row
measurement to the resulting computed `--syn-grid-row-block`.

The host also supplies true state through standard ARIA attributes
(`aria-selected`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-readonly`) and exposes
`data-syn-dirty="true"` and `data-syn-focused="true"` when applicable.
Do not derive permissions or errors from CSS.

Column headers and cells must be given **matching widths** by the host.
For virtualized rows, keep the virtualizer's measured/estimated row height
consistent with rendered CSS height. Keep the header inside the same horizontal
scroll container as the rows to prevent scroll drift.

Use `data-syn-density="compact"` only for visual spacing, not to change
virtualization row heights implicitly. For real grid widgets, the host must
implement a robust ARIA grid keyboard model and verify focus under virtualization,
including 400% zoom, forced colors, and screen reader behavior. Empty/loading and
paste error states need accessible descriptive text and focus management.

The optional CSS uses Syntyr's quiet operational surfaces by default; opt into
Grid/Noir palettes only when appropriate. Avoid glows or decorative motion
on data-heavy workspaces.

## Source: docs/recipes.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/recipes.md

# MIT-licensed composition recipes

For copyable input groups, labeled fields, container-responsive settings forms and optional headless UI styling, see [form composition recipes](component-recipes.md) and the [Radix adapter](radix-integration.md). For layered depth, incident-detail layouts, command presentation, timelines, and editorial product sections, see [premium compositions](premium-compositions.md).

These original Syntyr recipes are free to copy, edit, commercialize, and distribute under MIT. No Tailwind Plus source or premium assets were copied. For live examples see [the gallery](index.html), the [Grid console](../examples/console.html), and the [Noir pricing layout](../examples/pricing.html).

## Optional vertical flow

Use `.syn-flow` from `syntyr.recipes.css` on a content group to add
consistent gaps between adjacent **direct children**. The flex-column
composition stacks both inline and block elements, without overriding a
child component's own display. It does not globally reset margins or modify
unwrapped host markup. When children already have vertical margins, adjust
them at the application level to avoid unexpectedly large combined spacing.
For prose with heading rhythm, prefer the existing `.syn-prose` class.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-flow" style="--syn-flow-gap: 1.5rem">
    <h2 class="syn-section-heading">A native-first design system</h2>
    <p>Readable content with consistent configurable vertical rhythm.</p>
    <a href="/documentation">Read the documentation</a>
  </div>
</section>
```

`.syn-flow` is an opt-in composition, not part of the minimal core.
All spacing remains controlled by ordinary CSS custom properties.

## 1. Responsive telemetry cards

The `.syn-region` element establishes a **named inline-size container**. Unlike media queries, the cards respond to the width of the enclosing widget/sidebar. This is a native browser feature; no JavaScript observer is needed.

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-region" data-syn-theme="grid" aria-label="Network telemetry">
  <div class="syn-stats">
    <article class="syn-stat"><span class="syn-stat-label">UPTIME</span><p class="syn-stat-value">99.8%</p></article>
    <article class="syn-stat"><span class="syn-stat-label">NODES</span><p class="syn-stat-value">24</p></article>
    <article class="syn-stat"><span class="syn-stat-label">ALERTS</span><p class="syn-stat-value">02</p></article>
  </div>
</section>
```

## 2. Accessible empty state

```html
<section class="syn-empty" aria-labelledby="empty-heading">
  <p class="syn-eyebrow">QUEUE / EMPTY</p>
  <h2 id="empty-heading">No pending actions</h2>
  <p class="syn-muted">New items appear here once submitted.</p>
  <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/new">Create an item</a>
</section>
```

This is a *visual composition*, not a live queue implementation. Preserve real links, meaningful labels, and server-side behavior.

## 3. Three-card pricing display

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-region" data-syn-theme="noir" aria-label="Illustrative plans">
  <div class="syn-pricing">
    <article class="syn-price-card">
      <h2>Personal</h2>
      <p class="syn-price-value">$19<small> / month</small></p>
      <ul class="syn-feature-list"><li>One project</li><li>Basic support</li></ul>
      <a class="syn-button" href="/contact">Contact us</a>
    </article>
    <article class="syn-price-card" data-syn-featured>
      <h2>Studio</h2>
      <p class="syn-price-value">$49<small> / month</small></p>
      <ul class="syn-feature-list"><li>Unlimited projects</li><li>Team seats</li></ul>
      <a class="syn-button syn-button--primary" href="/contact">Contact us</a>
    </article>
    <article class="syn-price-card">
      <h2>Enterprise</h2>
      <p class="syn-price-value">Custom</p>
      <ul class="syn-feature-list"><li>Security review</li><li>Dedicated support</li></ul>
      <a class="syn-button" href="/contact">Contact us</a>
    </article>
  </div>
</section>
```

## 4. Stateful native button (host controlled)

```html
<button type="button" class="syn-button" aria-pressed="true">Grid view</button>
<button type="button" class="syn-button" aria-busy="true">Syncing status</button>
```

`aria-pressed="true"` conveys a real toggle state to accessibility APIs; set it only when a toggle actually is pressed. `aria-busy` signals that updates are in progress; it **does not** disable a button or create loading logic. The UI state must come from your application/server. If a state is only decorative, use `data-syn-state="active"` instead of misusing ARIA.

## Token-only custom theme

```css
/* Unlayered application CSS intentionally overrides Syntyr's layered tokens. */
.syn-root[data-syn-theme="custom"] {
  --syn-bg: #0b1019;
  --syn-surface: #192333;
  --syn-accent: #82f9d1;
  --syn-on-accent: #09120e;
  --syn-text: #eefbf7;
  --syn-muted: #bbd4ce;
  --syn-frame: #496b68;
}
```

For custom themes, test *every* textual token pairing and important state for WCAG contrast. The example overrides only a subset of the available color tokens and is not an accessibility certification.

## CRM and vertical SaaS patterns (alpha.5 source candidate)

Load `syntyr.core.css` and then optional `syntyr.recipes.css`. See the [complete CRM example](../examples/crm.html), which uses ordinary HTML and requires no JavaScript.

- **Filter bar:** `.syn-filter-bar` arranges labelled `.syn-filter-field` controls and a wrapping `.syn-filter-actions` group. Use `.syn-filter-field--query` for a wider search field. A `method="get"` form remains usable without JavaScript; the application must apply filters and preserve query values.
- **Pipeline:** `.syn-pipeline` contains named `section.syn-pipeline-lane` columns; each lane contains a semantic `ul.syn-pipeline-list` of `li.syn-pipeline-card`. Set `tabindex="0"` and an accessible name on the scrollable board so keyboard users can reach overflow. Links inside cards remain ordinary links. Drag-and-drop, permissions, saved filters, counts, and stage transitions must be implemented by the host application.
- **Record metadata:** `dl.syn-record-fields` groups each `dt` and `dd` in a direct child `div` for readable, responsive key/value pairs. Use a real `time` element for dates.
- **Density:** `data-syn-density="compact"` compresses control, row and card spacing without shrinking type. `data-syn-density="comfortable"` restores default metrics inside compact ancestors. `data-syn-density="spacious"` provides larger controls and rows for review-heavy screens. These attributes may be on `.syn-root` or nested elements. `comfortable` is the default when density is unspecified.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" data-syn-density="compact">
  <form class="syn-filter-bar" method="get" action="/opportunities">
    <label class="syn-label syn-filter-field syn-filter-field--query" for="crm-query">
      Search
      <input class="syn-input" id="crm-query" name="query" type="search">
    </label>
    <div class="syn-filter-actions">
      <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">Search</button>
    </div>
  </form>
  <div class="syn-pipeline" tabindex="0" aria-label="Opportunity stages">
    <section class="syn-pipeline-lane" aria-labelledby="crm-stage">
      <h2 id="crm-stage">Qualified</h2>
      <ul class="syn-pipeline-list">
        <li class="syn-pipeline-card"><a href="/opportunities/123">Example account</a></li>
      </ul>
    </section>
  </div>
  <section data-syn-density="spacious" aria-label="Opportunity details">
    <dl class="syn-record-fields">
      <div><dt>Owner</dt><dd>Account team</dd></div>
    </dl>
  </section>
</section>
```

The styles are layout primitives, not a grid widget or CRM engine. Keep keyboard focus visible, do not imply drag interactions, and render truthful stage counts. Preserve authorization and validate any user-controlled query parameters on the server.

## Reusing recipes across stacks

- **Go / templ, PHP, Django, Rust templates:** Make recipes server-rendered partials and pass content as arguments.
- **HTMX / Datastar:** Use the same classes on server-returned fragments. Their JavaScript, if chosen, is outside the CSS library.
- **React / Vue / Astro:** Wrap the exact markup in framework components only when the host application calls for it.

Favor stable component classes and CSS variables over copying long lists of generated utilities. See [contract](components.md) and [Tailwind research](tailwind-research.md).

## Accessible navigation and loading placeholders

Breadcrumbs use a real ordered list inside a labeled navigation landmark. The separator is a CSS border rather than spoken punctuation:

```html
<nav class="syn-breadcrumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><span aria-current="page">Reports</span></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

Page controls are **real links**, not inert buttons. Match the selected page to the actual URL, and label any symbol-only links:

```html
<nav class="syn-pagination" aria-label="Results pages">
  <a class="syn-page-link" href="?page=1">1</a>
  <a class="syn-page-link" href="?page=2" aria-current="page">2</a>
  <a class="syn-page-link" href="?page=3">3</a>
</nav>
```

Skeletons are deliberately static. Hide the visual placeholder from assistive technology and announce loading outside it with application-owned state. Do not leave an infinite loading message or use fake progress values:

```html
<section aria-busy="true" aria-label="Reports">
  <p role="status">Loading reports…</p>
  <span class="syn-skeleton" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="syn-skeleton syn-skeleton--short" aria-hidden="true"></span>
</section>
```

When loading finishes, the application replaces the placeholders with content and clears `aria-busy`. The CSS library does not implement fetching or state changes.

## Server-rendered SaaS filter and settings patterns

The [SaaS workflow demonstration](../examples/saas-workflows.html) shows how to combine standard HTML search forms, a table, navigation landmarks, native settings disclosures and no-JavaScript placeholders. The page's data is illustrative and **is not filtered**; the following behavior belongs to the host application:

- Parse and validate `query`, `status`, `owner` and `page` on the server, apply authorization before filtering, paginate the results, and escape all rendered user input.
- Preserve submitted form values and `aria-current` based on the actual result page, and emit a truthful result count plus empty-state or error message.
- Persist preferences in the server's settings endpoint, with CSRF protection for changes; the static demo intentionally has no save button.
- When using HTMX, Datastar or another enhancement layer, keep GET filters, ordinary links and form labels working without client-side JavaScript.

The scoped `examples/saas-workflows.css` stylesheet contains layout glue only and is **not** added to the distributed core or all-in-one bundle.


## Intrinsic responsive layouts (optional recipes CSS)

Load `syntyr.core.css` plus `syntyr.recipes.css`. The layout primitives are
scoped to `.syn-root` and require no JavaScript, framework or viewport media
queries. Their children are ordinary semantic HTML.

```html
<section class="syn-root">
  <div class="syn-sidebar" style="--syn-sidebar-width: 14rem">
    <aside>Navigation or filters</aside>
    <main>Main content</main>
  </div>
  <div class="syn-switcher" style="--syn-switcher-threshold: 42rem">
    <article>First card</article>
    <article>Second card</article>
    <article>Third card</article>
  </div>
</section>
```

`.syn-sidebar` expects **exactly two** direct children: sidebar first,
content second. Defaults: sidebar 16rem, content minimum 28rem (capped at
100% of available width). In narrow containers they stack, and neither
child is forced wider than the container by the layout primitive. Content
with long unbreakable text should still use appropriate wrapping.

`.syn-switcher` treats all direct children uniformly. Above the 40rem
default threshold they share a row; below it every child stacks. Override
`--syn-switcher-threshold` per instance. This differs from `.syn-grid`,
which can display different numbers of columns at intermediate widths.

Use opt-in fluid type classes `.syn-fluid-display`, `.syn-fluid-lede` and
`.syn-reading`. The CSS custom properties `--syn-fluid-display-size`,
`--syn-type-lede` and `--syn-reading-width` can be overridden in plain
application CSS. Keep real document headings and reading order.

See [the working minimalist demo](../examples/minimalist-patterns.html).


## Collection workspaces and error recovery (source candidate)

The optional recipes stylesheet contains `.syn-collection-toolbar`, `.syn-collection-actions`,
`.syn-bulk-actions`, `.syn-table--compact`, `.syn-result-state` and
`.syn-error-summary`. They extend the existing `.syn-filter-bar`, `.syn-table`,
`.syn-detail-layout` and base form classes; they do not ship a JS data grid.

[Static resource and error example](../examples/resource-workspace.html) demonstrates:
- A native GET search form with named query parameters (disabled in the static demo so it cannot navigate to an unimplemented route). Implement `/resources` on your server; the static example route does not filter results.
- A titled table, an optional dense presentation, explicit result states, and disabled bulk-action preview. The backend must enforce selection, authorization, CSRF and idempotency for mutations.
- A server-rendered error summary with field-anchor links, `aria-invalid`, and an `aria-describedby` reference to a visible field error. Preserve entered values and ensure the server response moves keyboard focus to the error summary after a failed submission (or sends an equivalent heading-focused full-page response). Never claim client-side styling performs validation.
- Preserve search/filter/sort state in URL parameters. Announce actual result counts, not sample counts. Display no-result or service-error state only when it is true.

The example is illustrative, **not a configured server**. Avoid relying on color alone to convey status. Test with a keyboard, screen reader, 320 CSS-pixel viewport, text zoom and forced-colors mode.

## Source: docs/component-recipes.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/component-recipes.md

# Copy-owned form recipes

These are **MIT-licensed, plain-HTML examples**. Copy and modify them without installing a Syntyr CLI, template registry, React, or a JavaScript runtime. Syntyr provides presentation; your browser and application provide behavior.

Load `dist/syntyr.core.css` and apply `.syn-root` on a stable ancestor. Input groups and fields are included in core. The examples below also work in Go/templ, Askama, Django templates, Astro, React, and HTMX.

## 1. Labeled field with assistance and server-side validation

```html
<div class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-field">
    <label class="syn-label" for="email">Work email</label>
    <input class="syn-input" id="email" name="email" type="email"
           autocomplete="email" aria-invalid="true"
           aria-describedby="email-help email-error" required>
    <p class="syn-help" id="email-help">Use your company email address.</p>
    <p class="syn-error" id="email-error">Enter a valid work email.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

Only render `aria-invalid="true"` and the error message when the form is actually invalid. Do not use CSS as a substitute for server-side validation. The field class groups presentation; the native `label for` association supplies the accessible name.

## 2. Search field with a connected button

```html
<search class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" aria-label="Search accounts">
  <form method="get" action="/accounts">
    <div class="syn-field">
      <label class="syn-label" for="account-query">Account name</label>
      <div class="syn-input-group">
        <input class="syn-input" id="account-query" name="q"
               type="search" placeholder="Search accounts">
        <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">Search</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>
</search>
```

This is **progressive enhancement**: the GET form submits with **No JavaScript**. An HTMX application may add `hx-get` and `hx-target` while preserving `action`, `method`, and a server-rendered fallback. The application must implement the endpoint and return actual search results.

## 3. Input addon (currency and unit)

```html
<div class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-field">
    <label class="syn-label" for="monthly-budget">Monthly budget (USD)</label>
    <div class="syn-input-group">
      <span class="syn-input-addon" aria-hidden="true">$</span>
      <input class="syn-input" id="monthly-budget" name="budget"
             type="number" min="0" step="0.01" inputmode="decimal">
      <span class="syn-input-addon" aria-hidden="true">USD</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

The unit is included in the label, not only in the decorative addon; assistive technologies must not depend on a symbol alone. Keep addons concise; overly long addons can compress their associated input.

## 4. Container-responsive horizontal form

```html
<form class="syn-root syn-region syn-form" action="/settings" method="post"
      data-syn-theme="corporate">
  <div class="syn-field-row">
    <label class="syn-label" for="org-name">Organization</label>
    <div class="syn-field-body">
      <input class="syn-input" id="org-name" name="organization"
             aria-describedby="org-help" required>
      <p class="syn-help" id="org-help">Visible to members of your team.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
```

The `syn-region` container determines whether rows become horizontal at 42rem. Without that ancestor they remain safely stacked. This is intentionally not a full grid/breakpoint framework. The help text is associated with its input via `aria-describedby`. A production POST endpoint must handle authorization, validation and CSRF.

## Optional companion styles

- [Radix Primitives state styling](radix-integration.md) provides an opt-in adapter for React applications while keeping Radix responsible for keyboard behavior.
- shadcn/ui components can adopt Syntyr tokens in application-owned CSS. Modern color variables can use values such as `--background: var(--syn-bg)` and `--foreground: var(--syn-text)`, **only when** the shadcn component expects complete CSS color values. Older `hsl(var(--background))` consumers require an HSL-channel bridge instead; do not apply the mappings blindly.
- `syntyr.semantic.css` remains a separate opt-in style for unclassed native HTML. Do not apply it indiscriminately around other component libraries.

See [the static form showcase](../examples/form-composition.html) and the [main component contract](components.md).

## Server-owned validation and local component variables (alpha.5 candidate)

Syntyr does **not** validate data, track touched fields, submit forms, or
announce errors automatically. The server should return the invalid form with
`aria-invalid="true"` on the affected field, an associated error via
`aria-describedby`, and optionally a visible error summary containing real
fragment links to the invalid fields. The browser's native `:user-invalid`
and `:user-valid` states style fields after user interaction where supported;
server-confirmed valid values may opt into
`data-syn-validation="valid"` (a **visual hint**, not ARIA and not proof).
Do not display success styling on untouched inputs. Never render an error
summary merely to hide it with CSS; omit it when the form is valid.

The optional `.syn-error-summary` class from `syntyr.recipes.css` leaves the summary visible and readable
in forced-colors mode. If the server inserts the message following a submit,
the host application determines focus, announcement and validation logic.

For one-off app themes, override **component-local CSS custom properties**
rather than selectors. Examples: `--syn-button-bg`,
`--syn-button-color`, `--syn-button-border-color`,
`--syn-button-hover-bg`, `--syn-panel-bg`,
`--syn-panel-border-color`, `--syn-field-bg`,
`--syn-field-border-color`, `--syn-field-valid-border-color`,
and `--syn-field-invalid-border-color`. All use existing Syntyr theme tokens
as fallbacks. Set the variables on the actual element or a containing
theme scope; they do not require Sass or JavaScript. For button color changes,
choose foreground/hover colors that meet applicable contrast requirements.

[See the static example with server-error, valid, disabled and token states](../examples/form-state-contracts.html).
