## Source: docs/native-patterns.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/native-patterns.md

# Native platform patterns and component imports

This prerelease Syntyr example uses original CSS, not upstream Blades source.
All patterns retain native HTML semantics and need **no runtime JavaScript**.
For a live static preview, see [the native recipe example (live alpha.5 source preview)](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/examples/native-recipes.html).

## Individually importable CSS

Use the following **source-tree alpha.5 candidate** entrypoints after this PR
is merged and released; they are not available in the published alpha.4 package:

~~~css
@import "@syntyr/css/components/tokens.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/base.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/buttons.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/forms.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/form-composition.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/overlays.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/native-recipes.css";
~~~

Every component CSS file is directly generated from its original source, using
the same order and cascade layers as core. Tokens, then base, then components,
then optional recipes is the supported loading order. Form-composition requires
forms. Do **not** load core and component entrypoints together, or styles will be
duplicated. Runtime CSS dependencies, imports and JavaScript are not included in
these distributables. In plain HTML, link the equivalent checked-in files under
the dist directory. Use version-pinned self-hosted assets in production.

If no selective loading is needed, use core plus the optional recipe sheet:

~~~html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.native-recipes.css">
~~~

## Native anchored popovers and modal commands

~~~html
<button type="button" class="syn-button" popovertarget="actions">Actions</button>
<div id="actions" popover class="syn-popover syn-popover--anchored">
  <a href="/settings">Settings</a>
</div>
<button type="button" class="syn-button" commandfor="report" command="show-modal">Report</button>
<dialog id="report" class="syn-dialog" aria-labelledby="report-title">
  <h2 id="report-title">Report</h2>
  <form method="dialog"><button type="submit">Close</button></form>
</dialog>
~~~

Native popover invokers provide an implicit CSS anchor in supporting browsers.
The anchored variant uses position-area plus block/inline flip candidates; in
other browsers it falls back to Syntyr's existing fixed corner positioning.
For vital actions, links remain real links. Modal invoker commands are not
universally available in older browsers, so provide a navigable fallback for
critical content or use a small explicit progressive enhancement in the host.
Transitions do **not** ship in core. To opt into native popover/dialog
motion, load the additional `syntyr.motion.css` file, then add
`.syn-popover--transition` to a `.syn-popover` or
`.syn-dialog--transition` to a `.syn-dialog`. Both class and file are
required. The motion module honors reduced-motion preferences; without
either opt-in, dialogs and popovers use their native static behavior.
Native browsers own focus management, Escape and dialog inertness; the stylesheet
does not implement a custom ARIA menu.

## Floating labels

~~~html
<div class="syn-field syn-field--floating">
  <input id="name" name="name" class="syn-input" placeholder=" " required>
  <label for="name" class="syn-floating-label">Full name</label>
</div>
~~~

Keep a persistent programmatic label with for/id. The one-space placeholder
is a deliberate :placeholder-shown state hook, **not** the accessible label.

The field becomes a **stacked, wrapping label above the input** when its own
container is narrow (21rem or less). This protects visible field identification
when users enlarge text, including long translated labels. At wider sizes the
floating presentation remains. The label is always a real `<label for>`; the
CSS never substitutes placeholders for an accessible name. Test real browser
zoom and translations in consuming applications.

Use only for text-like controls that implement placeholder-shown. Avoid for
date, color, select, checkbox, radio and unsupported types. Validate contrast
and long translated labels in the actual application.

## Semantic timelines and captioned code

~~~html
<ol class="syn-timeline" role="list">
  <li><time datetime="2026-11-15">15 November</time>Published</li>
</ol>

<figure class="syn-code-figure">
  <figcaption id="example-caption">example.go</figcaption>
  <pre tabindex="0" aria-labelledby="example-caption"><code>package main</code></pre>
</figure>
~~~

An ordered list communicates sequence; date/time labels are optional.
The figure gives code an authentic, accessible caption, and the focusable pre
supports keyboard scrolling of wide code samples.

## Server-rendering and framework use

- **Go templates and templ:** Emit the same native HTML; escape dynamic label,
  body and code text with the renderer and ensure stable unique id/for pairs.
- **Rust Askama:** Render this markup in a regular Askama template. Escape
  dynamic content; let forms submit to real routes.
- **Astro:** Import selected CSS files through its CSS pipeline, render standard
  HTML, and use Astro islands only for behaviors that require application state.
- **HTMX:** Keep popovertarget and commandfor on native controls; for actions
  that mutate data, use real forms/links and HTMX only as progressive enhancement.

### Go html/template

~~~html
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post">
  <div class="syn-field syn-field--floating">
    <input class="syn-input" id="profile-email" name="email"
           type="email" value="{{ .Email }}" placeholder=" " required>
    <label class="syn-floating-label" for="profile-email">Email address</label>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
~~~

The standard Go html/template engine escapes the Email value by context.

### Rust Askama

~~~html
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post">
  <div class="syn-field syn-field--floating">
    <input class="syn-input" id="profile-email" name="email"
           type="email" value="{{ email }}" placeholder=" " required>
    <label class="syn-floating-label" for="profile-email">Email address</label>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
~~~

Use Askama's HTML autoescaping, unique IDs when rendering multiple forms, and
normal server-side validation.

### Astro

~~~astro
---
import "@syntyr/css/components/tokens.css";
import "@syntyr/css/components/base.css";
import "@syntyr/css/components/buttons.css";
import "@syntyr/css/components/forms.css";
import "@syntyr/css/native-recipes.css";
---
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post">
  <div class="syn-root syn-field syn-field--floating">
    <input class="syn-input" id="astro-email" name="email"
           type="email" placeholder=" " required />
    <label class="syn-floating-label" for="astro-email">Email address</label>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
~~~

In a real Astro page place the syn-root scope around the entire page region,
as in this form. Package imports
are source candidate features until a corresponding npm release is published.

### HTMX (optional enhancement)

~~~html
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post"
      hx-post="/profile" hx-target="#profile-result" hx-swap="outerHTML">
  <label for="profile-email">Email address</label>
  <input class="syn-input" id="profile-email" name="email" type="email" required>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
<p id="profile-result" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p>
~~~

The action/method pair remains functional without HTMX. Host applications must
provide their own HTMX script and server response semantics.

This guide intentionally avoids wrappers and framework-specific JavaScript.
Refer to [framework integrations](framework-integrations.md) and the
[progressive enhancement guide (online)](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/progressive-enhancement.md) for host behavior
and fallbacks.

## Source: docs/radix-integration.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/radix-integration.md

# Optional Radix Primitives visual adapter

Syntyr core remains plain CSS with zero runtime JavaScript and zero React dependencies. Radix is a **separate application choice**. Its components own the accessible name, **ARIA** attributes, focus management, keyboard controls and state updates. Syntyr only adds styling.

## Install and opt in

In a React project using Radix Primitives, add a link **after** the core CSS:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/radix/states.css">
```

Copy [the adapter](../integrations/radix/states.css) into your project, or reference its repository source. Do not load it when you do not use Radix. It is **not** included in `syntyr.all.css`, either.

Wrap the relevant app area in `.syn-root`. Apply `.syn-radix` on that root, on a container inside it, **or directly on a stateful Syntyr control** to opt in only that control. If Radix portals content to the document body, set that portal's `container` inside the styled root, or style the portal explicitly. Do not assume portal content inherits Syntyr tokens when it is mounted outside the root.

## Example: controlled behavior, CSS presentation

```jsx
import * as Accordion from "@radix-ui/react-accordion";
import * as Toggle from "@radix-ui/react-toggle";

export function Controls() {
  return (
    <section className="syn-root syn-radix" data-syn-theme="studio">
      <Toggle.Root className="syn-button" aria-label="Pin dashboard">
        Pin dashboard
      </Toggle.Root>
      <Accordion.Root type="single" collapsible>
        <Accordion.Item value="filters">
          <Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Trigger className="syn-button syn-accordion-trigger">
              Advanced filters
            </Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className="syn-accordion-content">
            <p>Additional filters belong here.</p>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Radix supplies `data-state="on"`, `data-state="open"`, `data-state="closed"`, and `data-disabled` where applicable. The adapter consumes only those documented state hooks on **explicit Syntyr component classes**. It does not create a generic `data-state` styling API, and it does not replace Radix behavior.

## Accessibility and compatibility boundaries

- Test with keyboard only (Enter, Space, Arrow keys where appropriate, Escape) and screen readers; CSS passing a contract test is **not** an accessibility certification.
- Use a native button or Radix trigger for actions. Visual `[data-disabled]` states do not prevent click handlers from running; Radix/application logic must enforce disabled behavior.
- Preserve the focus-visible indication from Syntyr core and verify contrasts for all themes and custom token overrides.
- Avoid CSS-only emulations of focus traps, listbox navigation, complex comboboxes or dialogs.
- The adapter does not guarantee complete styling for every Radix primitive. Extend it with component-specific classes only when real use cases justify maintenance.

Related: [copy-owned component recipes](component-recipes.md), [framework integrations](framework-integrations.md).

## Source: docs/distribution.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/distribution.md

# Syntyr CSS distribution

**First time here?** Follow the [getting-started guide](getting-started.md) for one version-pinned stylesheet and a complete working page.

Syntyr CSS is MIT-licensed. No NPM install, JavaScript runtime, fonts,
icons, Sass compiler or CSS framework is required to use the distributed CSS.

## Recommended: self-host a versioned stylesheet

1. Download the asset from the [GitHub release](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/releases/tag/v0.3.0-alpha.4), or copy the matching file from the tag.
2. Put `syntyr.core.css` in your application's static CSS directory.
3. Load it normally:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Initialize</button>
</section>
```

The stylesheet's path is *your* path; mount or copy the file there.
The above works with Go templates, plain HTML, Astro, HTMX, React and other
renderers. See [the framework integration guide](framework-integrations.md) for
HTMX request-state classes, optional semantic markers, and server-side fragments. Add `syn-page` to the root only if you want full-page min-height.

## Offline SaaS preview in the next release ZIP (unreleased alpha.5)

The alpha.5 source candidate now packages `examples/saas.html` together with
`dist/syntyr.core.css` and `dist/syntyr.recipes.css`. After building or
extracting the **alpha.5** ZIP, open `examples/saas.html` directly in your
browser. Its relative stylesheets resolve within the extracted archive, so it
requires **no internet connection, local server, npm, build step or runtime
JavaScript**. You can edit the HTML and CSS locally to test integration.

This is a static **illustrative SaaS dashboard**: fictional metrics, no real
account data, authentication, filtering, API calls, or backend actions. To use
it in an application, replace sample values with server-rendered data and wire
navigation and mutations to your own server. The already published **alpha.4**
release does *not* contain this packaged example; the next alpha.5 release
has not been published yet.

## One-file semantic starter (unreleased alpha.5 source)

For a Pico-like HTML workflow, `dist/syntyr.semantic-bundle.css` combines core and semantic CSS into a single file. Copy it to your static assets, then opt in on the region you want styled:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.semantic-bundle.css">
<body class="syn-root syn-page syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <main class="syn-shell">
    <article><h1>Dashboard</h1><button type="button">Open</button></article>
  </main>
</body>
```

Only the controls and elements inside `.syn-root.syn-semantic` are styled semantically. This is **not** Pico's globally classless behavior: the root scope is deliberate. No script or build tool is required. [See the runnable starter](../examples/semantic-starter.html) and the [Pico migration guide](from-pico.md). **This file is not in the published alpha.4 release** and its `/dist/` URL is not an immutable release asset; pin a released version once alpha.5 is actually published. Do not load `core.css` or `semantic.css` alongside this bundle.

## Single-file presets (experimental alpha.5 source)

Choose one self-contained file and self-host it. There are **no stylesheet
imports or runtime dependencies**. Each preset includes tokens, core components,
and scoped opt-in semantic HTML styling:

| Preset | Distribution | When to choose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal | `dist/presets/minimal.css` | Documentation, forms and simple websites |
| SaaS | `dist/presets/saas.css` | Business sites, dashboards, HTMX/server-rendered apps; explicit `syn-u-*` helpers |
| Cinematic | `dist/presets/cinematic.css` | Optional Grid/Noir effects, precision frames, native CSS motion |

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr-saas.css">
<main class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <article><h1>Settings</h1><label for="email">Email</label>
    <input type="email" id="email" required>
    <button type="button">Preview</button>
  </article>
</main>
```

Only the path is application-defined; copy `dist/presets/saas.css` to match.
**Do not stack presets** or add core/semantic/recipes CSS already inside a
preset. Styles are still isolated to `.syn-root`, while bare element styling
requires `.syn-semantic`. Native dialogs/popovers/forms retain browser behavior;
Syntyr adds no component runtime. `data-syn-theme` and `--syn-*` custom
properties remain the theme API in every preset.

Advanced users can keep a single CSS output but omit unused core components
with the optional, stdlib-only `scripts/build_selective.py --components ...
--modules ... --output ...` build. That optimization is not a consumer
requirement and does **not** purge dynamic selectors or minify CSS.

`metadata/css-contract.v1.json` is a machine-readable, deterministic
**distribution artifact manifest**: it declares preset source order, file
names, raw/gzip bytes and SHA-256 hashes, together with the library version.
The `v1` suffix versions the **manifest schema**, not the public CSS API,
which remains experimental until an explicit v1 release. `build.py --check`
rejects stale CSS and contract manifests. See [CSS API stability](api-stability.md)
and [optional visual regression testing](visual-regression.md).

Try the [script-free preset demonstration](../examples/preset-preview.html).
This is present in the alpha.5 source candidate, **not published alpha.4**.

## Optional npm/package-manager distribution

A CSS-only `@syntyr/css` manifest is available in the alpha.5 repository candidate, but **it has not been published to npm**. See [package-manager installation and local tarball testing](package-managers.md) for supported imports and an explicit no-publication boundary. No package manager is required for the documented self-hosted stylesheet path.

## Optional themes and semantic HTML

Grid, Noir and Studio ship in the **same** core stylesheet; set
`data-syn-theme="grid"` or `data-syn-theme="noir"` or `data-syn-theme="studio"` on the scoped root.
You can nest differently themed elements.

The unreleased alpha.5 candidate adds Industrial, Terminal, Corporate and Minimal using the same scoped `data-syn-theme` contract. The published alpha.4 release includes Grid, Noir and Studio only.

Load `syntyr.semantic.css` after core **only** if you want automatic semantic
element styles within `.syn-semantic`. For static glows and decorative grid
effects, load `syntyr.effects.css` after core. SaaS, business and terminal layouts
are opt-in via `syntyr.recipes.css`. Optional frame geometry is in `syntyr.geometry.css`.
The alpha.5 working tree additionally provides `syntyr.utilities.css` for finite
layout helpers and `syntyr.print.css` for print-friendly reports. System-aware
Grid/Studio `data-syn-theme="auto"` is already included in core CSS, with
no additional stylesheet or runtime JavaScript. See the
[progressive-enhancement guide](progressive-enhancement.md) for examples.
The optional `syntyr.symbols.css` adds BYO-SVG icon sizing, literal Unicode styling and ASCII/box-drawing alignment without shipping fonts or icons; see [symbols and accessibility](symbols.md).

`syntyr.semantic-bundle.css` bundles core and semantic styles with scoped opt-in.
`syntyr.css` bundles core and effects. `syntyr.all.css` bundles all modules
while still requiring `.syn-semantic` to opt into semantic element styles.
Avoid loading these bundles alongside their component files: that duplicates CSS. Optional utilities live in the final `syn.utilities` cascade layer, allowing explicitly applied utility classes to override ordinary component declarations; see [the architecture policy](../ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Optional explicit selective build

Applications needing fewer core components can assemble a custom CSS file with
the Python standard-library-only `scripts/build_selective.py`. It does not scan
templates or purge individual selectors, and does not alter published assets.
See [selective builds and their limits](selective-builds.md).

## Pinned CDN for prototyping

```html
<link rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css">
```

The first-party Cloudflare CDN serves frozen, checksum-verified CSS releases
from a global edge network. Unversioned `/dist/` URLs can change with builds;
pin `/v/<version>/` instead. The documentation's optional theme editor
has JavaScript, but the library CSS and consumer sites do not require it.
For production applications, copying the versioned CSS to your own origin
usually avoids an additional hostname connection.

## Release artifacts and guarantees

The published alpha.4 release contains seven SYNTYR CSS distributions. The
unreleased alpha.5 source candidate includes modular SYNTYR distributions,
including the optional utilities, print and symbols stylesheets, plus
the terminal ANSI palette JSON, this guide, MIT license, and README. No retired compatibility aliases are shipped. The ZIP is created deterministically using only
Python's standard library:

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 scripts/package_release.py
```

Both visual themes and all essential components are MIT-licensed. Commercial
premium templates, if introduced, will be independently authored and sold
separately. This v0.3 alpha is **not** a v1 production compatibility guarantee;
cross-browser and full accessibility audits are still release gates.

The `syn-` selectors, `--syn-` custom properties and `data-syn-` attributes are the only supported source API.

## Source: docs/from-pico.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/from-pico.md

# Moving from Pico.css to Syntyr

**Syntyr is not a drop-in Pico replacement.** Both can style native HTML without
browser JavaScript, but they deliberately use different scoping, tokens and APIs.
Choose Syntyr for a scoped semantic mode that can grow into more elaborate SaaS
interfaces. Keep Pico (or use a compatible continuation) if globally classless
markup or exact Pico token compatibility is more important.

## Try a plain HTML page

In the **unreleased alpha.5 source candidate**, copy
`dist/syntyr.semantic-bundle.css` into your application's public CSS directory:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.semantic-bundle.css">
<body class="syn-root syn-page syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <main class="syn-shell">
    <article>
      <h1>Project settings</h1>
      <form action="/settings" method="post">
        <label for="title">Title <input id="title" name="title" required></label>
        <button type="submit">Save settings</button>
      </form>
    </article>
  </main>
</body>
```

The `/settings` action above is illustrative: your application must implement
its own backend, CSRF handling and persistence. For a fully static, runnable
example, see [the single-file starter](../examples/semantic-starter.html).

The current **published alpha.4** does not include the one-file semantic bundle.
For alpha.4, load `syntyr.core.css` followed by `syntyr.semantic.css` instead.
Do not combine either of those with the new one-file bundle: this duplicates CSS.

## Key differences

| Concern | Pico-style usage | Syntyr usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native HTML | Unclassed elements typically styled page-wide | `.syn-semantic` opt-in inside `.syn-root` |
| Page width | Conventional global container styles | `.syn-shell` on your layout container |
| Components | Small semantic-oriented API | Explicit `syn-*` classes when more control is needed |
| Themes | Pico's theme and palette variables | `data-syn-theme` and documented `--syn-*` tokens |
| Existing application CSS | Global rules can overlap | Scoped Syntyr selectors; check host/global resets |
| Interactions | HTML and application JavaScript | Native HTML and application JavaScript; no Syntyr widget runtime |

### Migration sequence

1. Choose a **small page or region**. Remove Pico's global stylesheet from
   that page where feasible, or carefully isolate the two frameworks.
2. Load the pinned Syntyr stylesheet and opt into `.syn-root.syn-semantic`.
   Without these classes, no Syntyr semantic styling is applied.
3. Keep real form labels, methods, actions, buttons, table headers, `details`
   and other native elements. Classless `form` and `fieldset` gain useful
   vertical layout in semantic mode; use `.syn-form` for the explicit class API.
   Add `.syn-shell` where a page-width constraint is useful.
4. Translate existing `--pico-*` customizations **by design role**, not by
   search-and-replace. Syntyr's `--syn-*` tokens are not one-to-one aliases.
5. If HTMX or another library adds temporary classes to formerly unclassed
   elements, prefer explicit `syn-*` component classes on published alpha.4.
   The `data-syn-semantic` marker is an **alpha.5-only** selector enhancement
   for retaining semantic styling through transient class changes; do not use
   it as an alpha.4 compatibility guarantee.
6. Run the optional `python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --semantic your-page.html`
   checker on literal HTML to catch labeling, reference and table-state mistakes.
   Dynamic templates still need rendered-page checks.
7. Test keyboard navigation, light/dark behavior, small screens, 200%/400%
   browser zoom, forced colors, and screen readers in the actual application.

## When not to migrate

Do not switch solely because Syntyr's stylesheet is small or has no JavaScript:
Pico, Tailwind-generated CSS, and other alternatives may have similarly low
browser runtime overhead. Syntyr's alpha status, unverified manual accessibility
gates, and different public API carry real migration costs. No measured
cross-framework performance advantage has been established.

See [distribution](distribution.md), [component contract](components.md),
[framework integrations](framework-integrations.md), and
[performance validation](performance-validation.md).

---

## Source: docs/api-stability.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/api-stability.md

# SYNTYR CSS public API and prerelease stability

**Status: experimental `0.3.0-alpha.5` candidate; no v1 stability promise.**
This document names the intended public contracts so that changes can be
reviewed consistently before `1.0.0`. It is not a new compatibility guarantee.

## Public surface and intended v1 boundaries

| Surface | Current policy | Intent for v1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `syntyr.core.css`, `.syn-root`, stable component classes | Public prerelease API | Stable selectors and behavior |
| New `.syn-field`, `.syn-field-row`, `.syn-field-body`, `.syn-input-group`, `.syn-input-addon` form compositions | Experimental prerelease core additions | Evaluate for v1 stabilization after browser/accessibility review |
| Documented `--syn-*` design-token names | Public prerelease API | Stable names, not fixed default values |
| `data-syn-theme` and documented `data-syn-*` state hooks | Public prerelease API | Stable names and meanings |
| `syntyr.semantic.css` and `.syn-semantic` | Opt-in prerelease API | Stable scoped semantics after audit |
| `dist/presets/{minimal,saas,cinematic}.css` | Experimental single-file entrypoints | Stabilize names and inclusion contract only after explicit review |
| `metadata/css-contract.v1.json` | Build artifact-manifest schema v1 | Version schema independently of public CSS API |
| `syntyr.recipes.css`, `syntyr.geometry.css` | Experimental, opt-in | Evaluate for individual stabilization |
| `syntyr.effects.css`, `syntyr.utilities.css` | Experimental, opt-in | Evaluate for individual stabilization |
| `syntyr.css`, `syntyr.all.css` | Public convenience bundles | Maintain documented contents/meaning at v1 |
| `terminal/palettes.json` | Optional example/palette asset | Separate compatibility decision from CSS |
| `integrations/`, `examples/`, documentation editor | Non-core adapters/showcases | No automatic CSS-core stability promise |

The `syn-*` selector namespace, `--syn-*` properties and `data-syn-*` attributes
remain the only Syntyr-specific styling namespace. ARIA states such as
`aria-pressed`, `aria-busy`, `aria-invalid` and native HTML state remain governed
by web-platform semantics, not a separate Syntyr state machine.

Core classes do **not** require an application build pipeline. The opt-in
semantic mode only styles elements under `.syn-semantic` within `.syn-root`.
Themes set design tokens; component selectors should not fork per theme. The
finite utilities are explicit overrides in their own final `syn.utilities`
cascade layer. Do not load a convenience bundle and its component modules
simultaneously.

### Alpha.5 opt-in CRM compositions and density profiles

The source-only `syntyr.recipes.css` adds optional `.syn-filter-bar`,
`.syn-pipeline` and `.syn-record-fields` compositions. These selectors are
experimental and are not in immutable alpha.4. Core adds explicit
`data-syn-density="comfortable"` and `"spacious"` profiles alongside the
existing `"compact"` profile, allowing nested density overrides.
No application behaviors or JavaScript are shipped with these compositions.

### Alpha.5 semantic HTML authoring changes

The unreleased semantic CSS candidate gives native classless `form` and
`fieldset` a composed vertical layout, a comfortable native `summary`
target, and readable table `caption` styling. Classed forms continue using
their explicit component API. For ordinary `.syn-table` rows,
`data-syn-state="selected"` remains the visual state; the
`aria-selected="true"` row selector now applies only to a real ARIA grid or
treegrid. Consumers styling ordinary table rows with `aria-selected` should
switch to the visual data attribute rather than inventing widget semantics.
The published immutable alpha.4 assets are unchanged.

The optional validator `--semantic` mode adds conservative native HTML
diagnostics, with no change to default validation or consumer runtime.

### Alpha.5 data-table wrapping migration

The unreleased alpha.5 candidate changes classed `.syn-table` cells to wrap
descriptive text by default, including when a table is placed in a narrow
container. This **prerelease layout compatibility change** may increase row
height in existing screens. To preserve the former implicit no-wrap behavior
for short codes, dates, or identifiers, explicitly add `.syn-cell--nowrap`
to those cells. Numeric cells with `.syn-cell--numeric` remain no-wrap.
Keep long prose wrapping whenever possible; if full columns require sideways
scrolling, use `.syn-table-wrap` with keyboard reachability and an accessible
table caption. The published immutable alpha.4 stylesheet is unchanged.

### Alpha.5 component-local styling and registry installation

In unreleased alpha.5, buttons, panels and form controls add optional,
inherited `--syn-button-*`, `--syn-panel-*` and `--syn-field-*`
custom-property overrides with their existing theme tokens as fallback.
Button variants do not require Sass or a separate compiled theme.
Server-supplied `data-syn-validation="valid"` is presentation-only; valid
and invalid states do not create validation, focus management, or ARIA
semantics. The existing opt-in `syn-error-summary` component remains
the supported form-level error presentation.

The source candidate includes an optional, **local-only** Python registry
planner. It resolves declared CSS dependencies and checks the current
source version, SHA-256 hashes and file collisions before any opt-in copy.
It does not fetch remote code, install a runtime or promise v1 API stability.

## Compatibility and version policy

- Before v1: breaking prerelease changes are possible; document them in the
  changelog. Do not maintain obsolete aliases solely for alpha compatibility.
- After v1: breaking changes to stabilized selector names, attribute meanings,
  documented file entrypoints and core component behavior require a major
  version. Additions can use minor releases; corrections use patch releases
  when semantically compatible.
- Values and appearance are not identical across patch versions. Accessibility
  fixes may adjust color, spacing, focus or contrast without renaming tokens.
- Custom, undocumented selectors and implementation variables are not a
  supported extension API. Use documented tokens and composition instead.
- Versioned `/v/<version>/` CDN assets remain byte-for-byte immutable; prefer
  self-hosting or pinning a version for production deployments.

## Pre-1.0 release checklist

1. Confirm which individual classes and tokens merit permanent compatibility.
2. Finish keyboard, screen-reader, browser zoom and contrast review; automated
   scans do not establish WCAG conformance.
3. Validate the supported browser/version matrix on realistic applications,
   including nested themes, CSS utilities and semantic opt-in behavior.
4. Publish versioned docs, a reproducible CSS distribution and a complete
   migration note if prerelease contracts change.

See [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md) for feature-admission criteria,
layer ownership and dependency boundaries. Optional package integrations may
provide additional contracts but must never introduce a mandatory core
runtime dependency.

---

## Source: docs/framework-integrations.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/framework-integrations.md

# Syntyr CSS integration guide: server-rendered HTML and frontend stacks

Syntyr is a **CSS presentation layer**, not a state manager, request client, or component runtime.
It has no JavaScript initialization, no required build tool, and no runtime dependency.
Every example uses the same `syn-` classes, CSS tokens and standard HTML.

## Choose one styling mode

1. **Explicit classes (recommended for apps):** load `syntyr.core.css`, use
   `.syn-root` on a stable ancestor, then `.syn-button`, `.syn-panel`, `.syn-input`, etc.
2. **Optional semantic HTML:** additionally load `syntyr.semantic.css` after core and
   add `.syn-semantic` to a scoped ancestor. Unclassed HTML receives semantic styles.
   For an element that an interaction framework will add classes to, opt it in once
   with `data-syn-semantic`. This preserves semantic styling while host-managed
   classes such as `htmx-request` are added and removed.

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <button data-syn-semantic hx-get="/status" hx-target="#status">Check status</button>
  <div id="status" aria-live="polite"></div>
</section>
```

**Host isolation:** Loading the CSS alone does not style a `.syn-button`,
`.syn-panel`, or other Syntyr class outside `.syn-root`. Existing host UI
components and CSS retain their presentation. Put `.syn-root` on the actual
Syntyr subtree (or on the component itself); do not assume a globally
scoped component class creates its own theme root. Syntyr uses native CSS
nesting for this boundary, so test embedding in each target browser.

The marker is only considered **inside** `.syn-semantic`, so it does not style
elements elsewhere. Do not put it on elements styled by a separate component
library unless you explicitly want Syntyr semantic styling there. Prefer
`.syn-button` for already-classed controls. The marker does **not** make the
control stateful, disabled, or accessible by itself.

For accessible advanced menus, comboboxes and toasts, see the [optional headless interaction guide](headless-interactions.md). All framework JavaScript remains application-owned.

## HTMX: progressive enhancement

A complete example with a real stdlib Python HTTP server is at:
[examples/htmx.html](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/htmx.html),
[examples/htmx_server.py](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/htmx_server.py), and
[examples/htmx.css](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/htmx.css).
These links lead to source files, not a live Cloudflare demonstration.

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 examples/htmx_server.py
# open http://127.0.0.1:8765/examples/htmx.html
```

The optional demo loads **pinned HTMX 2.0.8** from a third-party CDN. The CSS
library doesn't load HTMX automatically. Production applications should
self-host the pinned HTMX asset for control over performance, integrity, and CSP.

The search form uses a real `action` and `method=get`. When HTMX sends
`HX-Request: true`, the server returns only the result fragment. Ordinary
navigation gets a complete HTML document. The server emits `Vary: HX-Request`
to keep caches from mixing the representations, and escapes user-controlled
query text before inserting it in HTML.

For best results:

- Put `.syn-root` and `data-syn-theme` **outside** the swapped element.
- Swap the narrowest stable target (normally `innerHTML` inside a results container).
- Give labels and inputs stable IDs; preserve native form submission as a fallback.
- If a control must survive a larger swap, consider `hx-preserve` with a stable
  ID on both sides of the swap; prefer narrow targets first.
- Use the framework's `hx-indicator` and `hx-disabled-elt` when appropriate;
  `aria-busy` does **not** block duplicate submissions by itself.
- Do not create a permanent Syntyr HTMX runtime or register Syntyr lifecycle events.
- For strict CSP, use `includeIndicatorStyles: false` and an external stylesheet.
  The demo shows this pattern with a small **application-owned** `htmx.css`.
- Test initial document, request state, swapped fragment, form fallback, and
  failure paths in an actual browser.

The demo server intentionally exposes only four static assets and one GET route,
listens on localhost, and is **not** included in the Cloudflare static-site build.
A static host cannot serve its dynamic search endpoint without a backend.


## Server-driven HTML: optional request-state bridge

**No adapter is necessary to render Syntyr components.** Serve core CSS from
your application and output the same `syn-` classes in HEEx, Blade, ERB, templ,
Jinja, Twig or Razor. You only need a second CSS file if you want native
framework loading classes and attributes to show Syntyr's progress cursor:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.server.css">
```

Or, when using a CSS-aware package build system, import
`@syntyr/css/core.css` followed by `@syntyr/css/server.css`.
The optional `syntyr.server.css` is included in `syntyr.all.css`, but not core.
The npm package is an unreleased alpha.5 candidate; self-host prebuilt
files or a pinned release until that version is actually published.

The bridge is **presentation-only**. It styles the cursor on Syntyr buttons
during `data-loading`, `.htmx-request`, `.up-active`,
`.phx-click-loading`, `.phx-submit-loading`, `.phx-change-loading`, or
`[data-syn-state="loading"]`. It also supports `turbo-frame[busy]` and
request classes on enclosing HTMX, Unpoly and LiveView forms.
Datastar can explicitly bind `data-syn-state` to its own request-indicator
signal; Syntyr does not inspect or create Datastar signals. It never manages
`aria-busy`, disabled state, network requests, focus, announcements,
morphing, DOM lifecycle, or retries. Native disabled buttons retain
their disabled cursor; visual feedback does not block double submissions.

Keep `.syn-root` and `data-syn-theme` on a stable ancestor **outside**
the element that Turbo/HTMX replaces or that LiveView/Livewire morphs.
Prefer stable, unique input and form IDs. A server-rendered validation
message must use an associated `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`
on the input. Do not use `phx-update="ignore"` or `wire:ignore` just to
make styling survive framework patches.

## Phoenix LiveView (HEEx)

[Copyable HEEx form](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/server-rendered/liveview.heex)
uses the normal `phx-change` and `phx-submit` handlers. Server assigns
control the value and validation error:

```heex
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <form id="campaign-form" class="syn-form" phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save">
    <label class="syn-label" for="campaign-name">Campaign</label>
    <input id="campaign-name" class="syn-input" name="campaign[name]"
           value={@name} aria-invalid={if @error, do: "true", else: "false"} />
    <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit"
            phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save</button>
  </form>
</section>
```

LiveView adds `phx-submit-loading`, `phx-click-loading`, and
`phx-change-loading` to the relevant element or form while awaiting the
server. Its own `phx-disable-with` and form behavior handle interaction
locking; Syntyr never duplicates that logic. Include LiveView's ordinary
JavaScript bootstrap in your Phoenix application, not in Syntyr.

## Laravel Livewire (Blade)

[Copyable Blade form](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/server-rendered/livewire.blade.php)
uses `wire:submit`, `wire:model.live`, and Blade validation messages:

```blade
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <form class="syn-form" wire:submit="save">
    <label class="syn-label" for="campaign-name">Campaign</label>
    <input id="campaign-name" class="syn-input" wire:model.live="name"
           aria-invalid="{{ $errors->has('name') ? 'true' : 'false' }}" />
    <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="submit">Save</button>
  </form>
</section>
```

**Livewire 4** automatically adds `data-loading` to request-triggering
elements. Syntyr's optional CSS recognizes it without Tailwind. In
**Livewire 3**, use `wire:loading`, `wire:loading.attr="disabled"`,
or your own native `aria-busy`/`data-syn-state` binding where needed;
do not assume the v4 automatic attribute exists. For loading text,
prefer Livewire's own `wire:loading` and `wire:target` controls. Its
client runtime comes from the Laravel application.

## Rails Hotwire / Turbo Frames

[Copyable Turbo form](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/server-rendered/turbo.html)
uses a normal GET form to update only a matching frame. For a running
server-backed fixture with a real Turbo 8.0.23 browser integration,
see [examples/turbo.html](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/turbo.html)
and [examples/hypertext_server.py](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/hypertext_server.py):

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <form action="/campaigns" method="get" data-turbo-frame="campaign-results">
    <label for="q">Campaign</label>
    <input id="q" class="syn-input" name="q">
    <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Search</button>
  </form>
  <turbo-frame id="campaign-results"></turbo-frame>
</section>
```

The server must return a matching `<turbo-frame id="campaign-results">`
element. Turbo toggles `turbo-frame[busy]` while it fetches a replacement. The
optional CSS bridge styles enabled Syntyr buttons **inside** a busy frame;
for a button outside that frame, bind an application-owned
`data-syn-state="loading"` rather than expecting CSS to infer cross-frame
request ownership.
For the runnable example, start `python3 examples/hypertext_server.py` and
open `http://127.0.0.1:8767/examples/turbo.html`. The server distinguishes
`Turbo-Frame: customer-results` from native navigation, returns a matching
frame for enhanced requests, returns complete HTML for native GET requests,
and sets `Vary: Turbo-Frame` to avoid cross-representation caching issues.
The Turbo browser dependency is pinned and demo-only; self-host the bundle
in production. Syntyr never includes it.

Turbo Streams and full-page visits must keep the Syntyr root appropriately
scoped. Where Turbo must preserve a client-managed element, use
`data-turbo-permanent` with a stable unique ID on both versions. Do not put
an entire theme root inside a routinely replaced frame.
Forms with mutations still need application-owned authentication,
CSRF protection and server validation. This recipe does not ship Turbo.

## Go templ and other server template engines

[Copyable Go templ search template](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/server-rendered/search.templ)
shows a native GET form with escaped templ values. Serve the same CSS
from Go's static assets. The request handler performs the search and
renders the next HTML response; Syntyr does not add a Go dependency.

Django/Jinja, Symfony/Twig, ASP.NET Razor, Spring Thymeleaf, Hugo/Zola,
and other HTML renderers need no special integration: render actual
`<label>`, `<input>`, `<button>` and `<form>` elements with `syn-`
classes, apply `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` from server
validation, and keep static assets versioned. Choose framework-native
partials/components and anti-CSRF mechanisms.

**Verification scope:** the optional bridge and copyable templates have
Python standard-library contract tests. HTMX has an existing opt-in browser
suite; Datastar has an opt-in browser test using a pinned bundle.
Unpoly 3.15.0 and Turbo 8.0.23 have real, opt-in browser tests in
`tests/hypertext_browser.py` that cover request feedback, DOM replacement,
theme-root survival, and no-JavaScript form fallback in Chromium, Firefox
and WebKit (WebKit on a compatible Playwright container). The demo servers
also have request/response tests. This is **not** a claim that Phoenix,
Laravel, Rails, or Go application runtime tests have run. Add framework-owned
end-to-end tests when adopting templates.

## Lit / Web Components

Syntyr works with Lit but does not depend on it. Lit components using light DOM
can use ordinary `.syn-*` classes within a Syntyr root. Components with Shadow
DOM need local internal styles consuming inherited `--syn-*` tokens, and may
expose supported styling surfaces with `::part()`. Stylesheets in the page do
not automatically style the inside of a shadow root. See the
[Lit integration guide](lit-integration.md), [optional runnable example](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/tree/main/examples/lit)
and [component-authoring conventions](component-authoring.md).

## Alpine.js

Use native attributes for real state, and Syntyr classes for presentation:

```html
<div class="syn-root" x-data="{ selected: false }">
  <button class="syn-button" type="button"
          :aria-pressed="String(selected)" @click="selected = !selected">
    Toggle details
  </button>
</div>
```

Mount Alpine once in the host app. For `x-cloak`, define a tiny application
rule `[x-cloak] { display: none !important; }` before Alpine initializes.
Syntyr doesn't manage Alpine state.

## Datastar (signals + HTML/SSE morphing)

[Runnable Datastar example](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/datastar.html)
and [stdlib HTTP server](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/datastar_server.py)
demonstrate a real GET fallback and a Datastar SSE response:

```sh
python3 examples/datastar_server.py
# open http://127.0.0.1:8766/examples/datastar.html
```

The demo opts into a **pinned Datastar v1.0.5** browser script. That is an
application/demo dependency, not bundled or injected by Syntyr. Self-host the
pinned script in production.

```html
<main class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <form action="/customers/search" method="get"
        data-indicator:_fetching
        data-on:submit="!$_fetching && @get('/customers/search')"
        data-attr:aria-busy="String($_fetching)">
    <label class="syn-label" for="q">Customer</label>
    <input id="q" name="q" class="syn-input" data-bind:q>
    <button type="submit" class="syn-button"
            data-attr:disabled="$_fetching"
            data-attr:data-syn-state="$_fetching ? 'loading' : null">
      Search
    </button>
    <output role="status" data-show="$_fetching" style="display: none">
      Searching…
    </output>
  </form>
  <section id="customer-results" aria-live="polite"></section>
</main>
```

The framework owns `data-indicator`, `data-bind:q`, `data-on:submit`,
disabled state, and the SSE morph. The server returns
`event: datastar-patch-elements` with a matching `id="customer-results"`
and escapes user content. Because Datastar GET requests send signal values
inside a `datastar` query parameter, the sample endpoint reads that JSON for
SSE requests and reads ordinary `q` for no-JavaScript GET requests.

**Keep `.syn-root` and the form outside the morphed results section.**
Syntyr's `data-syn-state` bridge is optional; the native disabled state and
status message work independently of the progress cursor. Never rely on
`aria-busy` or a CSS class alone to prevent duplicate mutations.

Datastar expressions execute JavaScript. Do not interpolate untrusted data into
`data-*` expressions, do not put secrets in signals, validate on the server,
and adopt Datastar's documented nonce-based **CSP** mode when forbidding
`unsafe-eval`. Syntyr requires neither `unsafe-eval` nor a nonce.
Neither framework owns the other's initialization lifecycle.

## Unpoly

[Runnable Unpoly 3.15.0 demo](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/unpoly.html)
shares the [local HTTP server](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/hypertext_server.py)
with the Turbo demo. Run `python3 examples/hypertext_server.py` and open
`http://127.0.0.1:8767/examples/unpoly.html`.
The example pins the JS and CSS bundles; both belong to the demo application,
not Syntyr. Self-host both in production.

Unpoly adds `.up-active` to an initiating link or form and `.up-loading`
to the targeted fragment. Syntyr's optional `syntyr.server.css` styles the
progress cursor on an enabled `.syn-button.up-active` or the enabled
submit button inside `form.up-active`, without hiding, dimming, or blocking
the target. Unpoly owns response handling, loading feedback and morphing.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <form action="/customers" method="get" up-target="#customer-results">
    <label class="syn-label" for="customer-query">Customer</label>
    <input id="customer-query" class="syn-input" name="q">
    <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Search</button>
  </form>
  <div id="customer-results" aria-live="polite"></div>
</section>
```

The example server responds with an HTML document containing
`#customer-results`; Unpoly extracts and replaces the matching fragment.
Without JavaScript, a native GET responds with the same complete document.

Retain a real `action`, `method` and stable target ID. Keep the Syntyr root
outside any fragment Unpoly replaces; do not interpret `.up-loading` as a
reason to suppress keyboard interaction or hide results. Syntyr does not
include Unpoly or override its default CSS.

## React / Next.js

```jsx
import "./syntyr.core.css";

export function StatusCard({ status }) {
  return (
    <section className="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
      <article className="syn-panel">
        <h2 className="syn-heading">Operations</h2>
        <p>{status}</p>
      </article>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Import CSS once from the app entry point (or root layout, as supported by
the framework). No Syntyr provider, hooks, hydration, or dependency on React.

## Vue / Nuxt and Svelte / SvelteKit

Import the same CSS once. Bind native classes, `aria-*`, and
`data-syn-state` using each framework's built-in template syntax.
Do not wrap simple visual classes in additional runtime components unless the
application benefits from reusable semantic component boundaries.

## Astro, Hugo, Zola, Django, Rails, Go/templ and Rust templates

Serve `syntyr.core.css` as a normal static asset. Write HTML partials
with real headings, forms and links. Optional interactive islands can use
HTMX, Alpine, Datastar, React or native browser elements without changing
Syntyr's HTML/CSS contract. In Rails, Hotwire/Turbo updates have the same
theme-root and swap-boundary considerations as HTMX.

## Existing Tailwind or component-library applications

- Syntyr's `.syn-root` scope and `@layer syn.*` layers limit unintended
  interference, but Tailwind Preflight can still change global element defaults.
- Prefer explicit Syntyr classes. Apply `.syn-semantic` only to designated
  regions, not to a whole React/Headless UI component tree.
- Override public `--syn-*` tokens in application CSS; avoid copying or
  rebuilding utility frameworks inside Syntyr.
- Test cascade ordering, focus rings, dark/light color schemes, zoom and
  third-party components after integration.

## Performance and compatibility contract

- CSS bytes are tracked by `python3 scripts/asset_report.py` with optional JSON baseline comparisons; no arbitrary gzip release gate.
- Syntyr runtime JS: **zero**. HTMX/Alpine/React are host-app dependencies.
- Self-host assets on the app's own origin when practical; pin external CDN
  versions. Don't load both `syntyr.all.css` and its constituent stylesheets.
- Use Playwright or equivalent browser automation to verify dynamic class
  changes, HTMX fragments, responsiveness and accessibility.
- Avoid large DOM swaps, expensive decorative effects on scrolling tables,
  and unnecessary hydration. Measure actual page LCP, CLS and INP.

---

## Source: docs/native-browser-apis.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/native-browser-apis.md

# Native browser APIs in Syntyr

Syntyr is a styling system, **not** a browser API abstraction layer. It ships no runtime JavaScript or polyfill. Use the browser's built-in semantics and state before adding host-owned JavaScript. See the [scriptless integration demo](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/examples/native-apis.html) (source: `examples/native-apis.html`).

## Supported integrations

| Primitive | Syntyr integration | Fallback / requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTML Popover API | `.syn-popover` on `[popover]` with `popovertarget`/`popovertargetaction` controls | Native API requires modern browser; critical content should remain reachable another way for older browsers |
| Invoker Commands | `commandfor` and `command="show-modal"` on buttons targeting `.syn-dialog` | Older browsers may not support commands; give an ordinary link or `<details>` alternative |
| Native `<dialog>` | `.syn-dialog`, `form method="dialog"`, `closedby` or app-owned `requestClose()` | Never replace modal semantics with a popover; handle focus on open/close in real-app tests |
| CSS anchor positioning | `.syn-popover--anchored` alongside `.syn-popover` | With `position-area: bottom`, place near its invoking button; otherwise default to visible corner popover |
| Content-sized fields | `.syn-textarea--autosize` alongside `.syn-textarea` | `field-sizing: content` grows to a maximum height; normal resizable textarea remains functional without support |
| CSS scroll-driven animation | `.syn-reading-progress` in optional motion stylesheet | Decorative, hidden without support or with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` |
| Discrete overlay transitions | `.syn-popover--transition` in optional motion stylesheet | Uses `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`; no animation without support or when reduced motion is requested |
| Container queries | `.syn-region` with scoped layout patterns | Native responsive CSS replaces ResizeObserver for layout |
| Form constraint validation | `required`, native types, `:user-invalid` and optional `aria-invalid` | Application must provide meaningful feedback and accessible error text |

All new classes are **opt-in**. Core styles only add the anchor and textarea declarations; optional motion requires `syntyr.motion.css` (included in `syntyr.all.css`). Do not load `syntyr.all.css` alongside component files.

## Example: popover near its invoker

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.motion.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <button type="button" class="syn-button" popovertarget="account-menu">Account</button>
  <div id="account-menu" popover class="syn-popover syn-popover--anchored syn-popover--transition">
    <a href="/profile">Profile</a>
    <button type="button" popovertarget="account-menu" popovertargetaction="hide">Close</button>
  </div>
</section>
```

The invoker creates an implicit CSS anchor. Do not apply `position-anchor: auto` to unrelated floating elements; supply an explicit anchor relationship or use normal document positioning. The default `.syn-popover` remains visible in browsers without anchor positioning. Make sure production menus have sensible keyboard navigation and screen-reader labeling.

## Example: a dialog without an event handler

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="confirm-dialog" command="show-modal">Review</button>
<dialog id="confirm-dialog" class="syn-dialog" aria-labelledby="confirm-title">
  <h2 id="confirm-title">Review changes</h2>
  <form method="dialog"><button type="submit">Close</button></form>
</dialog>
```

The HTML Invoker Commands API is progressively available; don't assume the opener works in legacy browsers. A normal link to a review page or a `<details>` fallback gives users an accessible path even without it. Use `dialog.requestClose()` from host JavaScript when a cancelable close request is needed; unlike `dialog.close()`, `requestClose()` fires `cancel` first.

## Application-owned JavaScript (optional)

The following browser APIs are **not** included as Syntyr runtime dependencies. Use them only for capabilities CSS and HTML cannot provide:

- **View Transition API**: for same-document updates, use `document.startViewTransition(updateDOM)` only if present and if reduced-motion is not preferred; otherwise run `updateDOM()` directly. Cross-document navigation requires explicit `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` in *both* same-origin documents, not in a global Syntyr bundle. Preserve focus, history, and scrolling semantics during navigation.
- **Clipboard API**: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(text)` requires a secure context and permissions/user activation; catch rejections and provide a selectable text/link fallback.
- **Web Share API**: check `navigator.share`, invoke it from a click handler, catch cancellation or errors, and retain an ordinary shareable URL when unavailable. Do not assume mobile-only availability or guaranteed success.
- **ResizeObserver**: reserve for application logic that must know measured dimensions; use CSS container queries for styling. Avoid synchronous DOM changes from observers that trigger resize loops.
- **IntersectionObserver**: use to defer expensive application work, not for effects already supported by `animation-timeline: scroll(root block)`. Prefer native `loading="lazy"` for offscreen images and iframes.
- **Web Animations API**: suitable for interruptible, imperative application animations; use CSS transitions and scroll-driven animations for presentation-only changes and honor reduced motion.
- **Navigation API**: potentially helpful to app routers, but it changes navigation ownership. Do not add it to Syntyr just to style links; ordinary links work without it.

A safe view transition wrapper in application code, not the Syntyr library:

```js
function updateWithViewTransition(updateDOM) {
  if (!document.startViewTransition ||
      matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
    updateDOM();
    return;
  }
  document.startViewTransition(updateDOM);
}
```

## Browser-compatibility policy

Test Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit at narrow widths and 200%/400% zoom. CSS feature queries guard anchor placement and scroll-driven timelines. Without the advanced feature, the controls remain styled, dismissible, and operable **where the underlying HTML primitive is supported**. For genuinely older browsers that lack the HTML primitive entirely, provide an alternative interaction or a conditionally loaded host-app polyfill; Syntyr never silently installs one.

Always verify keyboard focus, Escape dismissal, forced-colors mode, native validation, and `prefers-reduced-motion`. Avoid animated content that conveys information unavailable as text. The scroll indicator uses `aria-hidden="true"` and must not replace a semantic progress bar for tasks.

Compatibility references: [Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API), [Invoker Commands](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API), [CSS anchor positioning](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_anchor_positioning), [field-sizing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/field-sizing), [scroll-driven animations](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_scroll-driven_animations), [View Transition API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API).
