## Source: docs/theme-customization.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/theme-customization.md

# Syntyr theme customization — copy, override, ship

Syntyr themes are **CSS custom properties**, not JavaScript configuration.
The MIT core already includes Grid and Noir palettes, responsive primitives,
accessible focus styling and semantic element options.

## 1. Choose a theme

Without a `data-syn-theme` attribute, `.syn-root` now uses Studio. Select Grid or Noir explicitly for technical/cinematic styles. This change is only in the unreleased alpha.5 candidate; version-pinned alpha.4 assets remain unchanged.

Load the published `syntyr.core.css` in your application and use regular HTML:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-panel--cut">
    <h2 class="syn-heading">Sector status</h2>
    <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Open</button>
  </article>
  <aside data-syn-theme="noir" class="syn-panel">
    Nested Noir preview
  </aside>
</section>
```

Use `data-syn-theme="noir"` for warm amber. Native HTML features
such as `details`, `dialog` and `popover` don't need framework JavaScript.

## 2. Override tokens using application CSS

Syntyr declares its defaults in named cascade layers. App CSS without a
layer takes precedence over layered author rules regardless of selector specificity.
Load application overrides **after** the Syntyr stylesheet to reduce surprises:

```css
/* app.css: original tokens, not copied from existing entertainment IP. */
.syn-root[data-syn-theme="grid"] {
  --syn-accent: #80dfef;
  --syn-on-accent: #07121a;
  --syn-accent-soft: rgb(128 223 239 / 10%);
  --syn-frame: #34576c;
}

/* Override one nested region without affecting the rest of the site. */
.my-warning-panel {
  --syn-surface: #1b232d;
  --syn-warning: #ffe2aa;
}
```

Important: `--syn-accent` is the most visible token, but `--syn-on-accent`
is the contrasting **foreground on primary buttons**. Change both when
necessary. Verify 4.5:1 contrast for body text and 3:1 for essential non-text
graphics; don't assume arbitrary overrides remain accessible.

Primary-button hover backgrounds default to the unchanged accent. On hover,
the border switches to the contrasting foreground for a visible affordance.
To customize the hover fill, set `--syn-primary-hover-bg` on the desired
theme/root and test its contrast with `--syn-on-accent` in both rest and hover
states. Syntyr does not automatically invent a contrast-safe hover color.

Use `.syn-panel--raised` for opt-in elevation. The `.syn-title`/`.syn-display`
and `.syn-section-heading` roles use native `text-wrap: balance` when
supported; unsupported browsers fall back to ordinary line wrapping.
Syntyr leaves platform font smoothing untouched.

Useful tokens:

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--syn-bg` | Main background |
| `--syn-surface`, `--syn-surface-hi` | Cards and controls |
| `--syn-text`, `--syn-muted` | Main and secondary text |
| `--syn-accent`, `--syn-on-accent`, `--syn-accent-soft` | Brand accent, its foreground, soft fill |
| `--syn-frame`, `--syn-danger`, `--syn-success`, `--syn-warning` | Borders and status |
| `--syn-font`, `--syn-mono`, `--syn-font-ui`, `--syn-font-display` | Body, technical, control, and display typography |
| `--syn-type-xs`, `--syn-type-sm`, `--syn-type-base` | Typography sizes |
| `--syn-surface-recessed`, `--syn-surface-raised`, `--syn-border-subtle` | Derived surfaces and quiet separators |
| `--syn-text-subtle`, `--syn-border-default`, `--syn-border-hover`, `--syn-border-focus`, `--syn-focus-ring` | Semantic text, borders, and focus |
| `--syn-surface-interactive`, `--syn-surface-hover`, `--syn-surface-pressed` | Theme-aware interactive control states |
| `--syn-primary-hover-bg` | Primary-button hover background; defaults to the accent so foreground contrast does not regress |
| `--syn-shadow-sm`, `--syn-shadow-raised`, `--syn-shadow-overlay` | Semantic elevation (small surfaces, raised panels, floating overlays) |
| `--syn-type-display`, `--syn-type-section`, `--syn-type-heading`, `--syn-type-body`, `--syn-leading-body`, `--syn-tracking-display` | Composable typography roles |
| `--syn-row-padding-block`, `--syn-card-padding`, `--syn-control-padding-block` | Density-aware spacing |
| `--syn-space-1` … `--syn-space-5` | Spacing |
| `--syn-cut`, `--syn-radius`, `--syn-control-height` | Geometry |
| `--syn-duration-fast`, `--syn-duration-standard`, `--syn-ease`, `--syn-ease-enter` | Optional transitions |
| `--syn-panel-padding`, `--syn-panel-radius`, `--syn-panel-border-width` | Local panel customization |
| `--syn-button-padding-inline`, `--syn-button-border-width` | Local button customization |

## 3. Independent visual intensity

Use `data-syn-intensity="quiet"` on a dense dashboard, the default `standard` for a balanced presentation, or `cinematic` on a limited hero region. Intensity controls only opt-in decoration in `syntyr.effects.css`; it does not alter palette, density, typography or control contrast. Nested regions can override an inherited value. See the [visual-intensity guide](visual-intensity.md) and [live comparison](../examples/intensity-geometry.html).

## 4. CSS component mode versus native semantic mode

Scoped component classes: `.syn-panel`, `.syn-button`, `.syn-table`.
They work with only `syntyr.core.css`.

For classless HTML resembling Pico CSS, load **both** files and opt in:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.semantic.css">
<div class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="noir">
  <article>
    <h2>Operator access</h2>
    <label for="operator">Operator ID</label>
    <input id="operator" name="operator" required>
    <button>Continue</button>
  </article>
</div>
```

Unclassed controls outside `.syn-semantic` are not restyled.
If you need glows or static grid effects, add `syntyr.effects.css`
as a third optional file. Don't load `syntyr.all.css` **and** its
individual component files at the same time.

## 5. Responsive applications and accessibility

Use `.syn-region` as the parent for container-responsive patterns such as
`.syn-stats`, `.syn-split`, `.syn-pricing`; width comes from the container,
not the whole viewport. Use `.syn-page` only for a full-page experience.

Syntyr also honors `prefers-contrast: more` by strengthening tokenized borders
and suppressing nonessential decorative effects, including inside nested
themes and explicit cinematic-intensity regions. This is a preference-aware
visual enhancement, not a substitute for actual high-contrast/forced-colors,
zoom, and screen-reader testing.

Syntyr honors `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Theme overrides
must not remove focus outlines, fake disabled states, or communicate state
only through color. Test keyboard navigation, 200%/400% browser zoom,
high-contrast/forced-colors, and relevant screen readers in the target app.

**No runtime JavaScript is required for styling.** Search, authentication,
live data, and server-side form handling are intentionally application
responsibilities; optional advanced widgets are outside the CSS core.

## Seven theme palettes (unreleased alpha.5 candidate)

The published alpha.4 tag offers Grid, Noir and Studio. This candidate adds Industrial, Terminal, Corporate and Minimal. Use the same HTML and change only the theme attribute:

- `data-syn-theme="grid"`
- `data-syn-theme="noir"`
- `data-syn-theme="studio"`
- `data-syn-theme="industrial"`
- `data-syn-theme="terminal"`
- `data-syn-theme="corporate"`
- `data-syn-theme="minimal"`

To use finite opt-in layout utilities, load `syntyr.utilities.css` after `syntyr.core.css` (or use the all bundle). Utilities include `.syn-u-flex`, `.syn-u-grid`, `.syn-u-between`, spacing helpers and a visually hidden helper. No compiler or runtime JavaScript is required.


## System palette, no JavaScript (experimental)

`data-syn-theme="auto"` on `.syn-root` or a nested themed region
uses Studio colors for light system preference and Grid colors for dark
system preference. It relies on native `color-scheme: light dark` and
CSS `light-dark()`, supported by current Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
Older engines that lack `light-dark()` retain the inherited/default
palette. No preference is stored or read by Syntyr.

```html
<body class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="auto">
  <section data-syn-theme="noir">This remains Noir regardless of OS theme.</section>
</body>
```

Explicit palettes are unchanged. For sensitive applications, test nested
themes, native form controls, and contrast in both OS preference modes.
## Typography, density, and quiet surfaces

Control and navigation text uses `--syn-font-ui`. Display headings use
`--syn-font-display`, while code and CLI regions retain `--syn-mono`.
Grid and Terminal choose monospace UI explicitly; Studio is the implicit default; light themes and Noir use
system sans-serif controls. Replace the font variables if a product has its
own typeface, without introducing required external fonts.

The `--syn-surface-recessed`, `--syn-surface-raised`, and
`--syn-border-subtle` tokens derive from the active theme palette and
recompute in nested themed regions. Strong borders remain available for
focus and essential controls. Avoid treating subtle separators as a substitute
for accessible non-text contrast where boundaries are required.

To opt into compact operational layouts:

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="minimal" data-syn-density="compact">
  <table class="syn-table"><!-- ... semantic rows ... --></table>
</section>
```

Compact density reduces padding and control heights, **not font sizes**.
Use the default density for content-heavy business pages or touch-first forms.
For an optional editorial hero, combine `syn-site-heading--editorial` from
`syntyr.recipes.css` with `syn-gradient-wash` from `syntyr.effects.css`.
Both use local fonts and static CSS without runtime dependencies.


## Semantic roles, states, and content rhythm

Use `.syn-display` (also available as `.syn-title`), `.syn-section-heading` for section titles, `.syn-heading` for card headings,
`.syn-body`, `.syn-text-support`, and the opt-in `.syn-prose` content
container. Typography roles inherit theme fonts and allow applications to
override type scale without rewriting individual component selectors.

Semantic aliases are derived separately in each nested `data-syn-theme`
scope, so a Grid panel inside a Studio page retains Grid's own contrast and
control appearance. To override theme colors, prefer changing the primitive
palette (`--syn-accent`, `--syn-frame`, `--syn-surface`, etc.). Override a
semantic role only when the change is intentional and contrast has been checked.

Native `disabled`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-busy`,
`:focus-visible`, and `:active` styles are presentation only. `aria-busy`
does not stop clicks or run a task. Use actual `disabled` for disabled form
controls; `aria-disabled` requires the application to suppress activation.
For errors, pair `aria-invalid="true"` with an associated error message
(`aria-describedby`); never rely on border color alone.

See [the live design-state example](../examples/design-states.html) for
semantic typography, nested themes, compact layout and form states.

---

## Source: docs/visual-intensity.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/visual-intensity.md

# Visual intensity and composable cyberpunk frames

SYNTYR separates **palette** (`data-syn-theme`), **decorative intensity**
(`data-syn-intensity`), **density** (`data-syn-density`) and optional geometry
(`.syn-frame` plus one shape). These are independent controls and do not load
JavaScript, fonts, sprites or third-party assets.

## Choose the right intensity

Use `data-syn-intensity` on `.syn-root` or any descendant element. It is
inherited, so a child can opt into a different intensity without switching
palette. Omitting the attribute is equivalent to `standard`.

| Value | Effects | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quiet` | Nearly invisible grids/washes; no visible glow/scanline overlay | Data-heavy SaaS, forms, accessibility-sensitive dashboards |
| `standard` | Existing effect strengths and opt-in behavior (default) | Marketing sites, documentation |
| `cinematic` | Stronger washes, luminous shadows and optional scanlines | Demos, editorial hero sections, limited promotional panels |

Intensity changes **only opt-in decorative effects** from
`syntyr.effects.css`. It does not change status colors, border contrast,
focus rings, typography, form affordances or any theme's underlying palette.
For zero decoration, simply do not load effects.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.effects.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geometry.css">

<main class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid" data-syn-intensity="quiet">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-glow">
    <h2>Operational view</h2>
    <p>Quiet default for dense data.</p>
  </article>
  <section data-syn-intensity="cinematic">
    <article class="syn-panel syn-glow syn-frame syn-frame--bevel syn-frame--accent">
      <h2>Featured transmission</h2>
      <p>A localized visual accent without changing colors or density.</p>
    </article>
  </section>
</main>
```

For custom presets, override `--syn-grid-alpha`, `--syn-glow-alpha`,
`--syn-wash-alpha`, `--syn-wash-secondary-alpha`,
`--syn-horizon-alpha`, and `--syn-scanline-alpha` on a region.
Values are percentages used in color interpolation, not animation speed.
Cinematic does **not** animate automatically; use optional motion modules
separately and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Geometry that composes

The optional `syntyr.geometry.css` stylesheet supports five shapes:
`bevel`, `notch`, `bracket`, `inset` and `circuit`.
Use exactly one shape on `.syn-frame`, optionally adding
`.syn-frame--accent` for a stronger outline (2px accent-colored border).
The geometry layer explicitly resets pseudo-element dimensions and clipping
from earlier CSS layers, so `.syn-panel--cut` on the **same host** is safely
superseded by the selected frame geometry rather than corrupting it.

```html
<article class="syn-panel syn-panel--cut syn-frame syn-frame--notch syn-frame--accent">
  <h2>System status</h2>
  <p>The notch frame takes precedence over the simpler panel cut.</p>
</article>
```

`syn-frame--accent` is an *optional* style modifier, not an additional
shape. Set `--syn-frame-cut`, `--syn-frame-stroke`,
`--syn-frame-fill` or `--syn-frame-outline` on the host to customize
one frame. Avoid combining two shape modifiers.

**Remaining composability boundary:** both `syn-frame` geometry and the
older `syn-frame--precision` recipe own `::before`. Applying both
to the same host still supersedes the precision accent; nest separate
elements when both treatments are needed. Likewise, geometry intentionally
uses a transparent host background so gradients painted on the **host**
may spill into its cut corners. Apply complex host backgrounds on an inner
element, or set `--syn-frame-fill` to a solid value.

## Accessibility and performance

- Always keep readable status text; never communicate errors only by glow or color.
- In forced-colors mode, frames fall back to solid system borders and effects
  suppress nonessential backgrounds.
- Prefer `quiet` for long operational pages; reserve `cinematic` for a few
  deliberate accents. Measure paint and scrolling on actual devices.
- The library core does not require any script. The optional docs theme editor
  can preview intensity but is not shipped as an application dependency.
- Test with 200% and 400% zoom, keyboard input, forced colors and all three
  browser engines before relying on a theme in production.

See [live intensity comparison](../examples/intensity-geometry.html),
[advanced geometry](geometry-terminal.md) and
[theme customization](theme-customization.md).

---

## Source: docs/visual-composition.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/visual-composition.md

# Syntyr visual composition — premium restraint, distinct character

This guide applies original layout decisions informed by the **principles**
publicly described by Resend, Vercel, Linear, Raycast and PostHog. Do not copy
their proprietary brand marks, code, fonts, illustrations, components or layouts.
The Syntyr CSS public contract stays independent and MIT licensed.

## Product-led presentation

- Show a real HTML/CSS component next to the markup used to construct it.
  Annotate fictional data honestly; never imply a static mockup is a live app.
- Use one dominant action and one secondary action in the first viewport.
  Move tertiary exploration paths to the next relevant section.
- Give each page one descriptive `h1`, readable section headings, and a clear
  keyboard-first navigation path. Do not rely on visual headings alone.

## Surface and typography rules

1. Prefer **one visible boundary per edge**. When nested surfaces both have
   borders, use `--syn-border-subtle` for internal dividers and reserve
   `--syn-frame` / `--syn-frame-strong` for controls and meaningful edges.
2. Apply depth sparingly. A raised overlay may use `--syn-shadow-overlay`;
   routine dashboard cards should rely on spacing and role separation first.
3. Use `--syn-font-ui` for ordinary controls, `--syn-font-display` for
   headings and `--syn-mono` for technical data. The optional system-serif
   editorial recipe should not bleed into operational controls.
4. Prefer sentence case for Studio, Minimal and Corporate UI. Technical
   uppercase labels are intentional in Grid and Terminal, not the default.
5. Use `--syn-accent` for real actions, selection, and a few signature
   details. Do not color every title, border, metric and icon at once.

## Same components, three visual directions

- [Studio operations](../examples/flagship-studio.html): compact density,
  unambiguous tables, quiet cards and a clear action order.
- [Noir editorial](../examples/flagship-noir.html): system serif, atmospheric
  background on one section, generous white space, restrained warm accents.
- [Grid control](../examples/flagship-grid.html): precise geometric framing,
  sparse cyan highlights, legible operational records and explicitly simulated
  output. Opt into cinematic effects only on a contained hero.

These are **documentation-only compositions**. Their `flagship.css` file is
application-owned showcase styling, not an additional required Syntyr module.

## Accessibility, motion and maintenance

- Maintain visible focus indicators and appropriate contrast for meaningful
  text and control boundaries; never depend on color, glow, or tiny labels alone.
- The data or state must still make sense at 320px and 400% zoom. Wide tables
  may scroll in a labeled, keyboard-focusable region.
- Suppress nonessential effects under forced-colors; respect reduced motion.
  Avoid perpetual `will-change`, large blur layers and decorative timers.
- Favor CSS custom properties and existing `syn-*` classes over bespoke
  component forks. Keep theme, density, intensity, and geometry independent.
- Measure real browser rendering and review screenshots before making
  visual regressions a release gate.

## References

Public design reading:
- [Resend brand guidelines](https://resend.com/handbook/design/what-are-our-brand-guidelines)
- [Linear design refresh](https://linear.app/now/behind-the-latest-design-refresh)
- [Vercel Geist design system](https://vercel.com/geist/introduction)

See also [theme customization](theme-customization.md),
[visual intensity](visual-intensity.md), and
[design research](design-research-linear-resend.md).

## Source: docs/geometry-terminal.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/geometry-terminal.md

# Advanced frames and terminal presentation

These are original, MIT-licensed SYNTYR CSS components. They do not replicate entertainment franchise assets or require JavaScript.

## Installation

Load only the modules you need. Advanced geometry is separate so ordinary pages do not load its CSS:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geometry.css">
<!-- Only for the optional application/terminal layouts: -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.recipes.css">
```

The all-in-one stylesheet includes geometry and recipes already. Do not load it alongside the individual modules.

## Seven independent frame profiles

Use `.syn-frame` with exactly **one** shape modifier. These can decorate an article, section, or any normal element. The surrounding content stays semantic:

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-frame syn-frame--bevel" style="--syn-frame-cut: 1.5rem">
    <h2>Monitoring</h2>
    <p>All systems operational.</p>
    <a href="/status">See status</a>
  </article>
</section>
```

| Class | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.syn-frame--bevel` | Diagonal cut on all four corners |
| `.syn-frame--notch` | Asymmetric top-right and bottom-left cuts |
| `.syn-frame--step` | Square stepped cuts on top-right and bottom-left |
| `.syn-frame--facet` | Diagonal cuts on top-left and bottom-right |
| `.syn-frame--bracket` | Four HUD-style L-shaped corner markers |
| `.syn-frame--inset` | Nested technical border |
| `.syn-frame--circuit` | Subtle corner trace bars |

These style variables are inherited and can be overridden on a specific panel:

- `--syn-frame-cut`: default `1rem`; fallback size for all cuts (backwards-compatible)
- `--syn-frame-cut-tl`, `--syn-frame-cut-tr`, `--syn-frame-cut-br`, `--syn-frame-cut-bl`: optional **Per-corner** overrides; use explicit CSS lengths
- `--syn-frame-stroke`: default `1px`; border thickness for clipped shapes
- `--syn-frame-fill`: default `var(--syn-surface)`; interior background
- `--syn-frame-outline`: default `var(--syn-frame-strong)`; solid border fallback
- `--syn-frame-border-paint`: optional color or CSS gradient for the complete border
- `--syn-frame-inlay-paint`: optional CSS gradient layered over the inner fill; use a translucent wash

The clipped shapes use individually corrected inner polygons to keep diagonal borders closer to their specified perpendicular stroke width. Square steps use the same step size for both polygons. These are **painted frames**, not clipped interactive hit regions; the native element remains a rectangle for layout and focus. Avoid cut sizes larger than the element can accommodate, or strokes as large as the cuts.

### Asymmetric geometry and gradient border example

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geometry.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-frame syn-frame--facet" style="
    --syn-frame-cut-tl: 1.5rem; --syn-frame-cut-br: .75rem;
    --syn-frame-stroke: 2px;
    --syn-frame-border-paint: linear-gradient(120deg, var(--syn-accent), var(--syn-frame-strong));
    --syn-frame-inlay-paint: linear-gradient(145deg, rgb(118 231 247 / 7%), transparent 65%);
  ">
    <h2>Signal analysis</h2>
    <p>Decorative geometry never replaces semantic content.</p>
  </article>
</section>
```

For the interactive **geometry editor**, open [Syntyr's component playground](playground.html#geometry-title). The playground JavaScript is documentation-only; consumers load only CSS. Existing bevel/notch markup retains its original appearance unless new controls are set, apart from the improved diagonal stroke geometry.

**Composition:** Advanced frame profiles own both pseudo-elements of the host node. They now reset the prior layer's corner dimensions and clip-path, so `.syn-panel--cut` can be used on the same element: the selected frame shape **supersedes** its simpler corner decoration. Add `.syn-frame--accent` for a stronger outline without adding any pseudo-elements. Do not combine multiple shape variants. The older `.syn-frame--precision` also owns `::before`; nest those two treatments if both accents must remain visible. The clipped border geometry does not depend on matching the parent background, but background gradients on the host can bleed into cut corners; prefer solid `--syn-frame-fill` or an inner element.

In forced-colors mode, decorative pseudo-elements disappear and a visible native border and Canvas background take over. Frames should not be the only way you communicate operational state.

## Browser terminal

Load `syntyr.recipes.css` for the existing `.syn-terminal` base and the additional presentation classes:

| Class | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `.syn-terminal-bar`, `.syn-terminal-title`, `.syn-terminal-dots` | Window chrome; mark visual-only dots `aria-hidden="true"` |
| `.syn-terminal-body`, `.syn-terminal-line`, `.syn-terminal-output` | Readable lines, wrapped output |
| `.syn-terminal-command`, `.syn-terminal-path`, `.syn-terminal-prompt` | CLI command anatomy |
| `.syn-terminal-success`, `.syn-terminal-warning`, `.syn-terminal-error` | Colored output (with textual status) |
| `.syn-terminal-meta`, `.syn-terminal-muted` | Secondary readouts |
| `.syn-terminal-cursor` | Static decorative caret; hide from accessibility APIs |

The terminal is **not** a shell emulator. It performs no input capture or commands. Applications implement real interaction separately; native CLI applications use `terminal/palettes.json` rather than browser CSS.

## Table and button behavior

The existing `.syn-table-emphasis` class highlights whichever cell you choose: there is no implicit highlight on the last column. Use `.syn-cell--numeric` on monetary or numeric cells for right-aligned tabular numbers.

The native HTML `disabled` attribute blocks button activation. The ARIA `aria-disabled="true"` attribute only communicates a disabled state; it **does not block activation**. Application/server code must enforce disabled behavior. CSS alone cannot guarantee it. For a disabled action that must remain discoverable to keyboard users, preserve focus and handle input appropriately.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 tests/browser_matrix.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit
```

See [the frame + terminal example](../examples/geometry-terminal.html). Browser checks are developer-only; the distributed CSS still has zero runtime JS or dependencies.

## Source: docs/viz.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/viz.md

# Syntyr Viz: optional, renderer-neutral charts

`syntyr.viz.css` is an **optional CSS-only presentation module**. It styles
charts and small, server-renderable data visualizations in all seven Syntyr
themes. It does not compute chart geometry, ingest data, perform interactions,
supply a JavaScript runtime, or require a frontend framework.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.viz.css">
```

Alternatively load `syntyr.all.css` by itself. Do **not** load the all-in-one
bundle together with component modules: it already includes Viz. Core, the
convenience `syntyr.css` bundle, and the optional recipes stylesheet do not
contain Viz.

## Chart token API

All visualization colors are CSS variables. Their defaults recompute on
`.syn-root` and nested `[data-syn-theme]` containers.

| Token | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--syn-chart-1` through `--syn-chart-4` | Data series colors, derived from theme accent, secondary accent, success, warning |
| `--syn-chart-grid` | Grid and chart cell border color |
| `--syn-chart-axis` | Axis labels and marks |
| `--syn-chart-tooltip-bg` | Noninteractive tooltip/popup surface |

Override the tokens on a specific themed chart or a nested dashboard area.
Always check contrast and series distinguishability after palette changes.
Color is not an adequate standalone representation of categories or status.
Use text, patterns, line types, legends and accessible values.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <figure class="syn-chart" style="--syn-chart-1: #2458c6;">
    <figcaption class="syn-chart-title">Weekly signups</figcaption>
    <!-- Supply SVG, a server-side renderer, or a client chart here. -->
  </figure>
</section>
```

## Four microvisualizations

### 1. SVG sparkline

`syn-viz-sparkline` styles a precomputed inline SVG. Syntyr does not calculate
points. For a time series, the HTML generator computes the polyline/area and
includes an accessible name. Use SVG `<title>` or `aria-label` and make the
numerical values inspectable in a nearby table or list.

```html
<figure class="syn-chart">
  <figcaption class="syn-chart-title">Revenue, Jan–Jun</figcaption>
  <svg class="syn-viz-sparkline" viewBox="0 0 240 60" role="img"
       aria-label="Revenue increased from 20 to 54 thousand dollars">
    <polyline class="syn-viz-sparkline-path"
              points="2,54 49,44 96,46 143,24 190,20 238,5"/>
  </svg>
  <table class="syn-table">
    <caption>Revenue by month, thousands of dollars</caption>
    <thead><tr><th scope="col">Month</th><th scope="col">Revenue</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody><tr><th scope="row">Jan</th><td>20</td></tr>
           <tr><th scope="row">Jun</th><td>54</td></tr></tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

### 2. Ranked bar list

Use real text for values; the bar widths are visual duplicates of the
values. `--syn-viz-value` is a number on a 0–100 scale, not a percentage
string. The CSS clamps it into that interval. **Validate and escape values
at the rendering boundary.** This is presentation only, not a semantic
`progress` or `meter` control.

```html
<ol class="syn-viz-bars" aria-label="Revenue mix">
  <li class="syn-viz-bar">
    <div class="syn-viz-bar-label">
      <span>Direct</span><data value="72">72%</data>
    </div>
    <div class="syn-viz-bar-track" aria-hidden="true">
      <span class="syn-viz-bar-fill" style="--syn-viz-value: 72"></span>
    </div>
  </li>
</ol>
```

### 3. Status tracker

This represents a series of discrete periods, not a live network monitor.
Each segment needs **real semantic text** even when a screen reader reads
its visual color differently.

```html
<ol class="syn-viz-tracker" aria-label="Past three days">
  <li data-syn-state="healthy"><span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Mon: Healthy</span></li>
  <li data-syn-state="degraded"><span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Tue: Degraded</span></li>
  <li data-syn-state="down"><span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Wed: Down</span></li>
</ol>
<p>Healthy, degraded and down states appear in chronological order.</p>
```

Supported state values are `healthy`, `degraded`, `down`, and `unknown`.
Do not depend on color alone to convey a critical state.

### 4. Activity heatmap

The heatmap is a compact grid. Set `--syn-viz-columns` to the number of
columns; each cell uses one of five levels, `0` through `4`.
The default is twelve columns. For small screens, the grid scrolls rather
than reducing each cell below its minimum width.

```html
<div class="syn-viz-heatmap" style="--syn-viz-columns: 3;"
     role="group" aria-label="Three days of activity">
  <span class="syn-viz-cell" data-syn-level="0">
    <span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Mon: no activity</span>
  </span>
  <span class="syn-viz-cell" data-syn-level="2">
    <span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Tue: medium activity</span>
  </span>
  <span class="syn-viz-cell" data-syn-level="4">
    <span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Wed: very high activity</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

## Generic chart styling and integrations

`syn-chart`, `syn-chart-title`, `syn-chart-grid`, `syn-chart-axis`,
`syn-chart-legend`, `syn-chart-legend-item`, `syn-chart-key` and
`syn-chart-tooltip` are **styling hooks only**. They never calculate axes,
create a legend, open a tooltip, or attach event handlers.

- **SVG/server-side:** generate SVG paths and visible, textual value tables
  with Go, Rust, HTMX, Python or any HTML renderer. All functionality remains
  available with no JavaScript.
- **Recharts:** set `className="syn-chart"` on your container and pass
  `var(--syn-chart-1)` etc. into the renderer's stroke/fill props. Use
  native Recharts tooltips/accessibility rather than expecting CSS to
  provide interactions.
- **ECharts:** ECharts needs resolved color strings in its JavaScript
  options, not literal CSS `var()` strings (Canvas cannot interpret them).
  Resolve scoped computed custom properties **inside an optional application
  adapter** and update them if the theme changes. Syntyr does not ship that
  adapter or make it a dependency.

## Accessibility and performance

Keep a visible title, visible value labels where possible, and a navigable
HTML table, list, or accessible summary for the underlying values. Verify
screen reader announcements, high-contrast/forced-colors mode, keyboard
navigation, and 200–400% zoom. Decorative SVG should be `aria-hidden` only
when equivalent numerical information exists elsewhere; meaningful SVG must
have a readable accessible name. Labels and patterns must distinguish status
independently of hue. The CSS includes forced-colors distinctions; test them
on the target browser rather than assuming automatic compliance.

All CSS is scoped under `.syn-root` and deliberately has no network assets,
fonts, animations, script tags or client-side data transforms. Syntyr Viz does
not impose arbitrary CSS size budgets. Use the library's existing deterministic
build and performance tests and measure real browser behavior.

Try the [seven-theme static Viz gallery](../examples/viz.html).

## Source: docs/accessibility.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/accessibility.md

# Syntyr CSS accessibility validation

**Status:** experimental alpha; not a WCAG certification or professional audit.

## Responsive follow-up — November 15, 2026

On the source merged by PR #135 (commit 0b04607), the published-site
layout suite passed **2,964/2,964** reflow cases: 76 allowlisted HTML
pages, 13 viewport/text configurations, and Chromium, Firefox, and pinned
Playwright 1.65.2 WebKit 27.2. These cover 320–1920 CSS-pixel widths,
mobile landscape, and 150%/200% root-text enlargement. This is **not**
native browser zoom.

For separate browser-UI zoom verification, an isolated X11 virtual display
was used to send the browser's native zoom keyboard shortcuts, rather than
CSS zoom, device emulation, or pinch/visual viewport scaling. Fourteen
representative pages passed at **200% and 400%** in both Chromium
(**28/28 checks**) and Firefox (**28/28 checks**): the original 1280
CSS-pixel viewport became 640 and 320 CSS pixels respectively, with
physical X11 window dimensions unchanged. The checks found no
document-level horizontal overflow or off-viewport controls. Pages
included the homepage, documentation, playground, pricing, forms, CRM,
console, Noir landing, and visualization gallery. Screenshots and
machine-local logs are test artifacts, not proof of a complete human
visual assessment. **Safari native zoom was not verified.**

The follow-up mobile audit identified ten native disclosure summaries with
19–22 CSS-pixel heights (three FAQ examples and seven chart data
expansions). A targeted change gives these standalone controls a 44px
minimum hit area at default text size, retaining native open/close and
focus behavior. The published-site browser matrix now checks native
controls for at least 24×24 CSS-pixel target geometry at 320px and 390px
unless a larger associated label supplies the target. This is a **focused
regression check**, not a full WCAG 2.2 target-spacing or touchscreen
conformance audit.

Manual assistive technology, Safari browser zoom, real hardware touch
testing, contrast exceptions, and native OS forced-colors review remain
outstanding.

## Audited source snapshot (November 15, 2026; commit `038a24d`)

At pinned `main` commit `038a24d`, deterministic CSS/metadata/adapters/site
checks passed, **311 Python contracts** passed, the **198-case**
Chromium/Firefox/WebKit page-viewport matrix and **264-case** enlarged-text
reflow matrix passed, alongside two simulated forced-colors checks and focused
native CSS tests; an independently executed **axe-core 4.10.3** audit of 21
pages returned **0 confirmed
automated violations but 129 unresolved color-contrast nodes**. The
candidate ZIP contains 39 files and is not a published release.

See the [exact-revision findings and manual-release blockers](accessibility-alpha5-review.md).
The 129 incomplete contrast targets require review. True browser zoom, OS
high-contrast, assistive technologies and independently executed exact-head
Woodpecker validation are **not** established by this snapshot. No WCAG
conformance or alpha.5 release approval is claimed.

## Historical post-merge results (November 14, 2026)

On `main` commit `b19c331` (after PRs #14 and #22), the Python suite
passed **155 tests**. The 16-page, three-viewport gallery matrix and 64
reflow cases per engine passed in Chromium **156.0.8078.4**, Firefox
**157.0**, and WebKit **27.2** using the pinned Playwright 1.64.1
Linux developer container. Twenty-three Chromium interaction
tests and the documentation theme-editor checks also passed.

axe-core 4.10.3 reported **zero confirmed automated violations** but
**345 inconclusive color-contrast element entries on 13 of 16 pages**.
These remain open for manual review. Live Cloudflare assets sampled against
the reproducible 63-file allowlisted build matched byte-for-byte; private
repository paths returned 404. Cloudflare's exact-head build passed, but
an independent Woodpecker pipeline execution has not been verified.

See [the current per-page evidence and manual gates](accessibility-alpha5-review.md).
This is not WCAG certification or verification of real zoom, screen-reader
behavior, or native OS high-contrast mode.

## What is and is not covered

- Source contracts: native HTML, semantic labels, opt-in scoping, predictable
  focus-visible outline, reduced-motion support, and forced-color hooks.
- Real browser matrix: Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit on desktop/mobile viewport widths,
  testing navigation, table semantics, native popover, disclosure, and overflow.
- Automated accessibility: axe-core WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A/AA tagged checks on the
  public showcase and example pages (the audited set changes over time). The tool may return
  **incomplete/manual-review** findings even with zero confirmed violations.
- Still needed: screen reader testing (NVDA + Firefox or Chrome, VoiceOver +
  Safari), actual browser zoom at 200% and 400%, touch target examination,
  interactive error states, font reflow and low-vision inspection.

## Reproduce the tests without installing production dependencies

Run the standard library contracts and optional Playwright checks:

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

# Dev-only installation; choose your package/environment manager.
python3 tests/browser_test.py
python3 tests/browser_matrix.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit
python3 tests/reflow_test.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit
python3 tests/published_reflow_browser.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit
python3 tests/minimalist_browser.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit
# Opt-in: seven-theme enlarged-label, scroll keyboard, and link-target checks.
python3 tests/accessibility_regression_browser.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit
```

For a pinned axe-core 4.10.3 audit, provide the checker at test time. No
JavaScript file is shipped to application consumers:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/axe-core/4.10.3/axe.min.js -o /tmp/axe.min.js
python3 tests/axe_audit.py --axe-file /tmp/axe.min.js \
  --report /tmp/syntyr-axe-manual-review.json
```

The published-site reflow test serves the actual Cloudflare-allowlisted HTML
and hashed CSS locally, checks every page in multiple portrait and landscape
viewports, and stresses root text at 150%/200%. It permits independently
scrollable data regions but rejects page-level horizontal overflow and
out-of-viewport controls. This is **not** 200%/400% native browser zoom.

For the remaining manual zoom gate, use the browser's own zoom control (not
CSS `zoom`, a changed root font size, device pixel ratio, or pinch zoom):
open the homepage, all-documentation index, free Noir landing, visualization
gallery, pricing, and native forms. Check 200% and 400% zoom at a 1280 CSS-pixel
starting window, then mobile landscape and portrait; record each browser,
OS, zoom, viewport, navigation/control reachability and any overflow. Run with
Chrome/Firefox and Safari/WebKit on a supported host, including keyboard and
screen-reader inspection. Keep these as outstanding human review requirements
until actually performed.

The JSON now includes a `summary` that distinguishes incomplete rule results
from **inconclusive individual element targets**, with counts by page and rule.
Prioritize the highest-count pages for composited-gradient and pseudo-element
contrast inspection. These targets are unresolved, not automatically passing
or failing; record measured contrast, viewport, state, and reviewer decision
before approving a release. The enlarged-label tests change root font size,
not genuine browser zoom; human zoom and screen-reader gates remain open.

## Contrast pixel triage (developer-only; NOT a conformance result)

An optional Chromium screenshot sampler helps prioritize axe-core findings that
cannot automatically evaluate gradients and pseudo-elements. It samples the
painted background under temporarily transparent glyphs, groups results by
page/viewport/selector, and retains non-text and unsampled targets explicitly.
The helper is deliberately **not a release gate**: selected pixels do not prove
the contrast of every glyph, hover/focus state, overlay or customized theme.
Run it with pinned tooling in a disposable developer environment:

```sh
python3 -m pip install playwright==1.65.2 Pillow==12.1.1
python3 tests/axe_audit.py --axe-file /tmp/axe.min.js \
  --report /tmp/syntyr-axe.json
python3 tests/contrast_pixel_triage.py \
  --axe-report /tmp/syntyr-axe.json \
  --output /tmp/syntyr-contrast-triage.json \
  --widths 1280 390 320
```

The November 15, 2026 `9ff10ac` baseline contained 162 incomplete contrast
elements. After rebasing the targeted contrast fixes onto `7e5c14d` (a newer
main with additional unrelated changes), a fresh axe scan reported **160
incomplete elements** across 27 pages. Across three widths (480 observations),
the heuristic classified 450 as sampled above their text threshold, 27 as
non-text (9 distinct targets), and 3 as unsampled placeholders (one distinct
target). **Zero samples fell below their threshold or within a 0.5:1 margin.**
The earlier 162-target and 456-above sample counts are historical; neither
report closes any axe incompletes as certified passes. Verify actual glyph
pixels, interaction states and screen reader/zoom/OS high-contrast behavior
before making a conformance claim.
Following a further rebase onto `c726dc3` (restored native-APIs page),
the newest candidate scan found **161 incomplete elements across 28 pages**:
450 text/viewport observations sampled above threshold, 27 non-text and six
unsampled textarea observations. There were still zero sampled-below or
narrow-margin observations. All 161 inconclusives remain open for manual
adjudication; the preceding 160-element count is historical.

See [the manual release review](accessibility-alpha5-review.md) for limitations.

For reproducible WebKit on an isolated testing host with Podman or Docker, clone
the repository to a directory that the container can read and run:

```sh
podman run --rm --shm-size=1g -v "$PWD":/work:ro,Z -w /work \
  mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.65.2-noble \
  bash -lc 'python3 -m pip install -q playwright==1.65.2 && \
    python3 tests/browser_matrix.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit && \
    python3 tests/reflow_test.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit'
```

The image supplies browser binaries and native dependencies, not the Python
Playwright package. This test-only container may download packages and should
be run against trusted code. The `:Z` mount flag is Podman/SELinux-specific;
adjust for Docker hosts. Keep the Python and browser versions aligned.

The remote URL is part of a **developer-only test**, not a browser runtime
dependency. Pin the checker release, review its MIT license, and verify its
provenance if incorporating it into build infrastructure.

## Earlier automated baseline (November 14, 2026, unreleased alpha.5)

Against post-merge `main` commit `6109b79`, an isolated Playwright v1.65.2
Linux container passed **126** page/viewport cases (14 pages × 3 widths × 3
engines) and **168** enlarged-text reflow cases (14 pages × 4 width/font
configurations × 3 engines). Browser-reported versions: Chromium
159.0.8154.6, Firefox 159.0 and WebKit 27.2. These versions describe a
specific passing test environment; they are not a promise of broader browser
support. Chromium additionally passed 17 interactive browser checks, two
simulated forced-colors checks and three documentation theme-editor viewport
checks in the developer environment.

The axe-core 4.10.3 WCAG-tagged scan found **0 confirmed automated violations**
across 14 pages, alongside **11 incomplete rule results encompassing 325
individual nodes**. Gradients, pseudo-elements and obscured backgrounds cause
most incomplete results; a missing automated verdict is **not** a passing
contrast measurement. Generate a selector-level local review list with:

```sh
python3 tests/axe_audit.py --axe-file /tmp/axe.min.js \
  --report /tmp/syntyr-axe-manual-review.json
```

A subsequent post-merge investigation of `4a623d0` confirmed that live
Cloudflare Pages serves identical CSS and selected documentation assets. A
supplemental Chromium pixel-sampling pass at 1280, 390 and 320 px found no
below-threshold contrast among **944 sampled element/viewport observations**
(19,689 background-pixel samples). The lowest was 4.65:1; a textarea's
placeholder was evaluated separately at 10.14:1. Sampling does **not**
resolve axe's 325 inconclusive color-contrast targets into certified passes.
See the detail and remaining exceptions in the review document.

See [`accessibility-alpha5-review.md`](accessibility-alpha5-review.md) for
per-page counts and the remaining manual release gates. In particular, the
browser harness modifies root font size; this is not equivalent to genuine
200%/400% browser zoom; simulated forced colors do not represent all native OS contrast modes;
and neither an axe scan nor automated keyboard actions constitute screen-reader
validation. Native HTML dialog invoker command support also varies by browser.

## Manual checklist

1. Tab from the top of every page; test visible focus, no keyboard traps and
   skip-link behavior. Open and dismiss popovers/dialogs with keyboard.
2. At 200% and 400% zoom, inspect all content at narrow widths; no clipped
   actions, invisible labels or lost table information.
3. Test one screen reader per major browser engine for headings, landmarks,
   table captions, form labels and live status; document the actual device,
   browser version and assistive technology.
4. Force-colors/high-contrast: check panel separation, focus and form controls.
5. Disable animations in system settings and ensure nothing depends on motion.
6. Validate both the default Grid/Noir palettes and any project-specific
   token overrides for text contrast and non-text essential indicators.


## Optional system palette and intrinsic layout checks

The [minimalist patterns example](../examples/minimalist-patterns.html)
uses a CSS-only `auto` palette (Studio for light, Grid for dark),
classless form controls and intrinsic layouts. Its optional browser test
checks both OS color-scheme emulations, an explicit nested Noir region,
native checkbox/radio label layout, keyboard focus and mobile wrapping.

These automated checks do **not** replace manual audits at actual 200% and
400% browser zoom, assistive-technology operation, or customized palette
contrast validation. Record browser engine and OS when testing these paths.

## Experimental native-HTML semantic coverage (unreleased branch)

The optional `syntyr.semantic.css` now also presents native `search`, `figure`, `figcaption`,
`mark`, `kbd`, `output`, `meter` and scrollable `pre` regions. These styles apply
only inside an opted-in `.syn-semantic` subtree and do not implement
application behavior.

The development-only `tests/native_semantic_browser.py` checks Chromium,
Firefox and WebKit at 320px and 900px: the `mark` foreground/background pair
has at least 4.5:1 computed contrast in seven named palettes and automatic
light/dark mode; forced-colors emulation keeps it distinguishable; the native
GET form works without JavaScript; removing `.syn-root` removes the styling.
At 320px it checks horizontal document overflow with 200% and 400% *root
font-size enlargement*, including a scrollable code block.

These tests are **not** actual browser 200%/400% zoom, manual OS high-contrast
inspection, NVDA/VoiceOver validation, or a WCAG conformance audit. The
pre-existing inconclusive axe contrast cases and manual release gates remain
open. Use the separate [native example](../examples/native-elements.html)
for representative manual checks after publishing.

## Post-merge native-element review follow-up (November 15, 2026)

The native HTML example received four confirmed actionable review findings after
PR #38 merged. The follow-up fixes make its horizontally scrollable `pre`
region keyboard-focusable with an accessible name/region role, allow long `kbd`
chords to wrap, preserve readable foreground color for `mark > code`, and
strengthen the browser regression to verify actual internal scrolling and
keyboard focus instead of merely checking `scrollWidth >= clientWidth`.

Reproducible checks on the follow-up worktree:

- New unit contracts: 11 native-element tests pass; the full stdlib suite
  passed 189 tests before final documentation/rebase.
- Developer-only Playwright smoke: Chromium, Firefox, WebKit each passed
  across seven themes, light/dark auto, 320px/900px widths, forced-colors
  emulation, 200%/400% root-font enlargement and keyboard access to the
  scrollable SQL example.
- Shared browser matrix: all three engines passed 18 pages at three viewports.
- Shared reflow matrix: all three engines completed 72 checks each (216 total).
- Pinned axe-core 4.10.3 audit: **0 confirmed automated violations**, with
  **10 incomplete rule checks** across the 18 included pages. The new
  `examples/native-elements.html` page reported 0 violations and 0
  incomplete checks. Other pages' inconclusive findings remain manual-review
  items; these results are not blanket color-contrast certification.

### Outstanding human validation (not yet performed)

1. With **VoiceOver + Safari** and **NVDA + Firefox/Chrome** (Orca + Firefox
   can be supplementary on Linux), navigate to
   [the native HTML example](../examples/native-elements.html); verify the
   "SQL query example" region is named, focusable with Tab, and responds to
   horizontal scroll keys, without trapping focus.
2. In a real browser, set **200% and 400% browser zoom**, not only the root
   font-size test harness. At a 320 CSS-pixel effective viewport, verify
   readable captions, long keyboard shortcuts, full access to the code
   example, visible focus and no clipped form action.
3. With an actual OS high-contrast/forced-colors mode, distinguish highlights,
   focus rings, and selected controls. Also examine all axe inconclusive
   contrast targets from the main release accessibility report.
4. Record device, assistive technology version, browser version, observed
   behavior, any defects, and reviewer sign-off before claiming WCAG
   conformance or closing the manual release gate.

These are QA instructions, not evidence that human assistive-technology or
browser-UI zoom testing has happened.

## Searchable component catalog coverage (November 15, 2026)

The documentation-only component catalog has been added to the normal browser,
reflow, and axe-core matrices rather than relying only on static contracts.
It contains ten rendered component examples. With JavaScript disabled, the
examples and native HTML source disclosures remain available. Enhanced search,
empty state, live result count and clipboard/keyboard fallback were checked
in both Chromium and Firefox.

Exact-branch developer-only verification:

- Chromium and Firefox: **19 pages × 3 viewports** each, including the catalog
  interactions, passed.
- Chromium and Firefox: **76 enlarged-root-font reflow cases per engine**
  passed. This is **not** genuine browser-UI zoom.
- Local axe-core: **zero confirmed automated violations** across the 19
  audited pages, with **10 incomplete rule checks** requiring manual review.
  The catalog contributed one incomplete color-contrast rule with two nodes
  in the featured pricing demo: axe cannot infer its gradient background.
- For the catalog Studio palette, a source-token-based conservative calculation
  gives approximately **13.79:1** for dark #15233a text against the strongest
  9% blue-accent overlay on white. This is theoretical CSS compositing, not
  sampled pixels or a conformance certification.
- WebKit was **not** validated on this exact branch: the Gertrude test host
  lacks libevent-2.1.so.7.

The remaining release gates are genuine browser 200%/400% zoom, screen readers,
native high-contrast inspection, and manual resolution of incomplete axe
targets. Do not present these findings as WCAG conformance certification.

Optional native recipe smoke test: run `node tests/native_recipes_browser.js` with developer-installed Playwright and its browser engines. It exercises form label state, popover escape/dismissal, modal commands where supported, reduced-motion transitions, and narrow viewport reflow. No Playwright package is shipped to consumers.

## Source: docs/agent-integration.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/agent-integration.md

# Using Syntyr with coding agents

Syntyr works with ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code, Cursor and other agents that generate HTML or framework markup. No Syntyr-specific service, account, MCP server or runtime JavaScript is required.

## Recommended context to supply an agent

1. Specify **the exact Syntyr release and CSS modules installed** (published `0.3.0-alpha.4` versus unreleased source `0.3.0-alpha.5`).
2. Link to [AI quickstart](ai-quickstart.md) and the relevant [component reference](components.md). If the agent can fetch websites, include [`/llms.txt`](../llms.txt).
3. For complex UI, supply [recipes](recipes.md), [framework integrations](framework-integrations.md) and the [component manifest](../metadata/components.json). For unreleased alpha.5 source-only form patterns, use [copy-owned form recipes](component-recipes.md) and the optional [Radix styling adapter](radix-integration.md); do not attribute these to published alpha.4.
4. Ask it to state which stylesheets it used, avoid undocumented classes and verify keyboard/form semantics.

Suggested prompt for an existing application:

> Use Syntyr CSS to build a responsive, accessible account dashboard. My app uses the published v0.3.0-alpha.4 core and recipes CSS, with Studio as the theme. Read the Syntyr AI quickstart and relevant component docs. Generate semantic HTML compatible with my framework. Use only classes present in those stylesheets; if a needed component is unavailable, compose native HTML with application CSS instead. Keep data, auth and actions in the host app. Return the necessary markup, CSS links and a list of any custom styles.

## Project-level integration

A consumer may copy [`agents/syntyr/SKILL.md`](../agents/syntyr/SKILL.md) as an optional local skill in agent tooling that supports Skills. It is a portable instruction document, **not a published package, automatic installation, or guaranteed discovery mechanism**.

The repository's root `AGENTS.md` guides agents contributing to Syntyr itself. It does **not** automatically become instructions in a separate application repository.

## Offline first-run agent setup (source checkout)

An optional Python standard-library command installs a **portable consumer Skill**,
release-pinned CSS, and a small verified selector reference into an existing app.
It runs from a Syntyr source checkout and does **not** install any application
runtime dependencies, connect to services, or publish a package:

```sh
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py init --project /path/to/my-app --format json
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py check --project /path/to/my-app --format json /path/to/my-app/page.html
# The source-checkout helper remains available without the experimental CLI:
python3 scripts/syntyr_agent.py check --project /path/to/my-app --json /path/to/my-app/page.html
```

`init` defaults to the **published, immutable alpha.4 CSS** and writes
`syntyr.agent.json`, versioned CSS files under `vendor/syntyr/<release>/`,
and `.agents/skills/syntyr/SKILL.md` plus `references/api.json`. Rerunning is
idempotent. Different existing files or symlinked output paths are rejected
without overwriting project content. For tooling that expects another skill
location, specify `--agent claude` or `--agent cursor`; `--agent codex` and
`--agent generic` use the portable `.agents/skills/` path. Projects must still
load the copied CSS in their own HTML/framework entrypoint: installation does
**not** silently modify application code or guarantee CSS integration.

Choose `--release 0.3.0-alpha.5` only when deliberately testing the
**unreleased source candidate**. The generated `api.json` lists selectors
actually present in the selected CSS files; source-only selectors cannot
appear in an alpha.4 reference.

`check` validates the installed CSS asset hashes and literal `.html` files
against that project's pinned release, returning structured, source-located
JSON diagnostics. Its exit codes are **0** for checked and error-free HTML,
**1** for errors, and **2** for incomplete coverage (for example, JSX/TSX/Vue/Svelte
or no HTML files). The first framework-aware layer reports static selector
errors inside literal JSX/Vue/Svelte opening tags, but it deliberately leaves
these files unverified: dynamic bindings and actual framework syntax require
proper parsers and browser tests. It is not a React/Vue/Svelte parser or a
browser accessibility test. Generated CSS assets are not proof that the app has actually imported
them. The separate local MCP adapter remains available for smaller markup
fragments and interactive catalog queries.

## Optional local MCP adapter

An optional **read-only local MCP server** can now expose the checked-in
component catalog and CSS API to supported coding agents. It is not needed to
use Syntyr CSS, is not installed by the npm package, and does not expose a
hosted endpoint. See the [MCP adapter source and installation guide](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/tree/main/agent_mcp)
for the separate Python SDK installation, version-safe tools, and limits.
It defaults to the published immutable `0.3.0-alpha.4` CSS rather than
silently offering source-only `0.3.0-alpha.5` selectors. The read-only
`validate_markup` tool reuses the [static checker](editor-integration.md#optional-static-html-diagnostics)
for source-located, machine-readable errors, available class suggestions, and
valid theme/state values. Responses are constrained to the selected release's
checked-in CSS rather than presenting candidate-only selectors as fixes.

## Documents and machine-readable inventory

- [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt): small navigation file following the community `llms.txt` convention; it is useful when deliberately retrieved, but not a universal automatic-discovery protocol.
- [`llms-full.txt`](../llms-full.txt): generated, version-stamped concatenation of selected public technical docs, for tools that benefit from one context file.
- [`metadata/components.json`](../metadata/components.json): small **curated, non-exhaustive** inventory with the CSS modules required by the included classes. Do not infer that a class is unavailable solely because this catalog omits it.
- [`metadata/syntyr-contract.json`](../metadata/syntyr-contract.json): full source-discovered Syntyr classes, tokens, known stylesheet distributions, themes, literal state values and curated component recipes. This candidate-version manifest is suitable for LLM tooling and optional [static HTML checks](editor-integration.md#optional-static-html-diagnostics); it is not a compiler or an accessibility certification.

Documentation follows the current source candidate; always check [release boundaries](api-stability.md) and the [distribution guide](distribution.md) before using candidate-only features.

## Documentation formats: HTML for people, Markdown for agents

Every approved public guide is published at two stable paths. Use the readable HTML page (for example, [`/docs/components.html`](components.html)) in browser navigation, search results and links to end users. Use the original Markdown (`/docs/components.md`) for coding-agent retrieval, repository editing and `llms.txt` references. The [complete HTML guide directory](reference.html) is the human entry point. Both formats contain the same authored guide content; the HTML is rendered ahead of time, not by client-side JavaScript.

These are **different representations of the same public documentation**, not user-agent cloaking. Anyone can request Markdown directly; agents can also read HTML. Markdown responses have a `text/markdown` content type and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` so search engines favor HTML, while `robots.txt` and the sitemap advertise public HTML pages. Do not disallow Markdown in `robots.txt`: agents need to fetch it explicitly. HTML has canonical URLs and points back to its Markdown source via `rel="alternate" type="text/markdown"`.

When adding a guide for public consumption, review the explicit `PUBLIC_DOCS` allowlist in `scripts/build_cloudflare_site.py`. Regenerate the committed HTML with the maintainer-only generator (`python3 scripts/build_doc_pages.py`), and verify it with `--check`. The core static-site and CI builds require no Markdown parsing package or client runtime.

## Validation and maintenance

The repository uses Python standard-library scripts:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_agent_docs.py --check
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 scripts/build_cloudflare_site.py --check
```

The consolidated reference is deterministic and checked in CI through the Python test suite. The Cloudflare publisher uses a strict allowlist, so exposing new documentation does not expose internal files or business planning documents.

## What Syntyr does not do

Syntyr styles browser HTML/CSS. It does not supply a JavaScript component runtime, chart rendering engine, AI API, CRUD handlers, form submission or remote data access. The optional local read-only MCP adapter is a separate developer tool, never a CSS runtime dependency. Use your existing application technology for those responsibilities.

---

## Source: docs/editor-integration.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/editor-integration.md

# Syntyr editor autocomplete and metadata

Syntyr's editor integration is **optional**. Applications still consume ordinary
prebuilt CSS, HTML, and custom properties without Node, JavaScript, or a build step.

## VS Code and compatible editors

For an opt-in local extension package that bundles these files without an extension runtime, see [ecosystem interoperability](ecosystem-integrations.md). The extension is not yet published to the VS Code Marketplace; the manual workspace integration below remains supported.

Copy these four generated files from the Syntyr release or repository into
your project, e.g. `./vendor/syntyr/metadata/`:

- `syntyr.html-custom-data.json` — HTML attribute values, including themes
- `syntyr.css-custom-data.json` — documented `--syn-*` custom properties
- `syntyr.code-snippets` — a curated set of class completion snippets
- `syntyr-api.json` — complete machine-readable index of classes, tokens and themes

Add the following to your **workspace** `.vscode/settings.json` (not required
for Syntyr consumers using other editors):

```json
{
  "html.customData": ["./vendor/syntyr/metadata/syntyr.html-custom-data.json"],
  "css.customData": ["./vendor/syntyr/metadata/syntyr.css-custom-data.json"]
}
```

Optionally copy `syntyr.code-snippets` to `.vscode/syntyr.code-snippets`.
This provides snippets for common `syn-*` classes in HTML and JSX/TSX. The
custom HTML data includes all classes as possible `class` attribute values,
but the extent of **class-name completion** varies by editor and extension;
do not assume it works identically in every language mode. CSS custom
property autocomplete also depends on the editor's CSS language support.

The JSON files are standard, inspectable data; other editors and integrations
can consume `syntyr-api.json` directly.

## Regenerate after CSS changes

From the Syntyr source repository:

```sh
python3 scripts/export_api_metadata.py
python3 scripts/export_api_metadata.py --check
```

The Python standard-library exporter scans `src/**/*.css`, strips comments,
deduplicates discovered classes and declared custom properties, adds
documented component override variables, and writes stable JSON and snippets.
`--check` fails if the checked-in outputs differ from source. Descriptions
are curated for core APIs and source-file-derived for others.

This is an editor convenience layer, **not** a Tailwind-style CSS compiler.
A class being present in the metadata does not mean its optional stylesheet
is already loaded. Check each item's `module` in the generated catalog and
load the corresponding Syntyr CSS distribution.

## Optional CSS dependency and version diagnostics

Syntyr can also diagnose duplicate stylesheet links, overlapping distribution
bundles (for example, `syntyr.core.css` loaded with
`syntyr.semantic-bundle.css`), and conflicting explicit release pins:

```sh
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --doctor --semantic index.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --doctor --format json index.html
```

The `--doctor` flag builds on the existing validator; it does not install or
change CSS. It reads the generated `distribution_sources` from
`metadata/syntyr-contract.json`, which comes from the canonical CSS build
registry. Keep the checker, metadata, and stylesheet release versions together.
Older contracts without this field are rejected instead of silently missing
overlaps.

An overlapping bundle, including a duplicated stylesheet, produces a
**warning** (exit code 0 if no errors). Two different explicit
`/v/<version>/` release pins produce an **error** (exit code 1), since
mixing different Syntyr releases is unsafe. Generated diagnostics include
filename, source position, severity, code and explanation. Normal validation
without `--doctor` is unchanged.

**Scope:** This is a static HTML check of Syntyr `<link rel="stylesheet">`
references. It does not infer versions for unpinned local assets, parse CSS
`@import` graphs, or inspect imports inside JS/TS build pipelines. When
using bundlers, validate the final loaded stylesheets and run browser tests.
Unknown host-application CSS is ignored. Duplicate warnings are advisory;
releases still need actual cross-browser and accessibility verification.

## Optional static HTML diagnostics

The generated `metadata/syntyr-contract.json` is Syntyr's machine-readable
development contract. It combines the **full source-discovered** class and token
inventory with the existing **curated** semantic component recipes, supported
theme/state values, and CSS distribution filenames. The contract is generated
by `python3 scripts/export_api_metadata.py` and checked by `--check`. Do
not edit it directly. The existing `metadata/components.json` remains a
curated subset and is not a complete list of classes.

The unreleased alpha.5 release ZIP candidate now includes both `scripts/syntyr_check.py` and its matching `metadata/syntyr-contract.json`, so the extracted archive can run the optional checker without a source checkout. The published alpha.4 ZIP does not include these tools.

To validate static HTML during development (Python 3.10+, standard library only):

```sh
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py index.html examples/saas.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --format json index.html
# Opt-in, conservative native HTML checks (warnings do not fail the CLI):
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --semantic --format json examples/semantic-starter.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --stylesheets syntyr.core.css,syntyr.recipes.css partial.html
# Pipe generated markup into the same deterministic checker without a temporary file:
printf '<button class="syn-buttn">Save</button>' | python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --format json -
# For fragments, supply the CSS modules actually installed in the consumer app:
cat fragment.html | python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --format json --stylesheets syntyr.core.css -
```

### Agent-ready composition recipes

The same generated `metadata/syntyr-contract.json` includes an optional
`recipes` array curated in `metadata/components.json`. Each recipe declares:

- A stable `id`, purpose, example page and required CSS distributions.
- A native HTML `root` element and named `slots` with `tag`, `classes`,
  `optional` and `repeatable` fields.
- `variants` restricted to real, CSS-supported `data-syn-*` attribute values.
- `host_behavior` explaining what CSS **cannot** perform (server requests,
  selection, pagination, validation, focus or authorization).

Available recipes cover a CRM filter form, semantic resource table, app shell,
and validated form. Use a `.syn-root` ancestor for every composition, and load
all listed stylesheets in the documented order (core before optional recipes).
The contract's `slots` describe roles, **not a strict DOM nesting validator**;
authors must still use accessible native HTML in context. The host application
supplies state and behavior. No JavaScript component engine is required.

Source truth is the existing curated `metadata/components.json`, not another
hand-maintained metadata registry. After editing a recipe, run
`python3 scripts/export_api_metadata.py` to regenerate the contract;
`python3 scripts/export_api_metadata.py --check` detects drift. The exporter
rejects stale class names, missing CSS modules, unsupported variant values,
invalid example paths and duplicate slot names before publication.

The checker reports source positions, unknown literal `syn-*` classes, invalid
literal `data-syn-*` values, and missing optional CSS modules **when a Syntyr
stylesheet is linked or explicitly specified**. For full HTML documents with
an explicit `<html>` element, it also reports `unscoped-class` when a known
Syntyr component class is outside every `.syn-root` ancestor. Since CSS
selectors are scoped, those classes would otherwise silently render without
Syntyr styles. Plain HTML fragments are exempt because the embedding app may
supply the root; dynamic ancestor classes and inert `<template>` contents are
also exempt because their rendered scope is unknown.

With `--semantic`, a second standard-library pass checks literal HTML for
duplicate static IDs, missing form labels, unmatched `label for` and
`aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` ID references (the latter two only in
complete documents). It advises when an ordinary table row uses
`aria-selected` instead of `data-syn-state`, or when a headed data table
lacks a caption or other accessible name. Errors produce exit code 1; advisory
warnings are included in text/JSON output but do not fail the command unless
`--fail-on warning` is explicitly supplied for strict CI.
The mode is **off by default** to preserve existing integrations.

This is not an HTML conformance parser, a WCAG audit, or a template renderer.
It deliberately skips inert template content and avoids guessing what dynamic
attributes resolve to. Validate rendered server/framework templates and actual
screen-reader behavior separately. Static fragments may reference IDs supplied
by their embedding document, so cross-document references are checked only
when a full `<html>` document is supplied.

The checker recognizes local and version-pinned stylesheet paths (including
query parameters). Without a known Syntyr stylesheet, module-presence checks
are skipped, but root-scope checks still run for complete documents. Explicit
`--stylesheets` overrides stylesheet-link discovery.

Exit code 0 means no errors (including warnings-only), 1 means one or more
errors, and 2 means invalid arguments or unreadable files. Explicit
`--fail-on warning` makes warnings exit 1 as well. JSON diagnostics contain `file`, `line`,
`column`, `severity`, `code` and `message` fields. Input `-` reads HTML
from standard input and identifies findings with `file: "<stdin>"`; JSON stays
a top-level diagnostics array for backward compatibility. Agent-friendly
optional fields include `suggestions` (up to three real source-contract class
names with available stylesheet distributions), `class_name` and
`required_root` (unscoped component classes), `attribute` and
`allowed_values` (invalid theme or state), and `required_stylesheets` and
`loaded_stylesheets` (missing CSS modules). Suggestions are hints, **not**
automatic edits; confirm the target class exists in the **installed** release.

**Boundaries:** This is a static HTML checker, not a full HTML accessibility
auditor, runtime type checker, or an HTML/CSS build requirement. Dynamic
template class expressions are conservatively skipped. Component `elements`
describe composite examples rather than allowed tags for every constituent
class; the validator deliberately does not enforce those as strict rules.
JSX/TSX, HEEx, Blade, and Nulang template adapters would need separate
language-aware parsing. Semantic accessibility and actual loaded CSS still
need browser and keyboard checks. No script or generated manifest is shipped
to the browser by this integration.

---

## Source: docs/cli.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/cli.md

# Optional Syntyr CLI (alpha.5 source candidate)

**Syntyr CSS never requires a CLI, Python, Node.js or application JavaScript.**
The developer-only CLI runs offline on Python 3.10+ and never executes registry
markup. It is distributed separately from the CSS ZIP.

## Run from the source tree

```sh
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py version
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py init --project /path/to/app --format json
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py check --project /path/to/app --format json /path/to/app/page.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py list --category blocks
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py add resource-workspace --project /path/to/app
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py add resource-workspace --project /path/to/app --apply
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py verify --project /path/to/app
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py check --semantic --format json path/to/index.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py check --semantic --fail-on warning path/to/index.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py doctor --format json path/to/index.html
python3 scripts/syntyr_cli.py doctor --fail-on warning path/to/index.html
```

The default add operation is a **read-only preview**. Installation requires
explicit `--apply`. It creates assets only under the project's
`syntyr/` directory and records SHA-256 hashes and installed items in
`syntyr.lock.json`. Repeated installs of identical assets are safe.
Modified or unexpected existing files are not overwritten. An installation
failure rolls back only unchanged files created by that invocation.

`syntyr verify` compares installed bytes with the lockfile, returning
exit code 0 when clean, 1 when content has drifted, or 2 for an invalid/
missing lockfile or command error. Resolve drift manually before adding items.
There is deliberately no force, upgrade, remote fetch, execute or delete command.
Manual customization is supported, but doing so breaks strict managed-file
verification until you intentionally reconcile the lockfile.

`syntyr init` is an **optional offline consumer-agent setup**, separate from
`syntyr add`: it copies immutable published alpha.4 CSS, a portable
`.agents/skills/syntyr/SKILL.md` with release-pinned selector data, and
`syntyr.agent.json` into an existing project. This defaults to published
`0.3.0-alpha.4`, not the CLI's unreleased alpha.5 source candidate. Override
with `--release 0.3.0-alpha.5` only when deliberately testing the unreleased
source CSS. Use `--agent claude` or `--agent cursor` for those opt-in skill
locations. Existing differing files and symlinked output paths are refused;
no application imports are edited automatically.

`syntyr check --project /path/to/app` verifies the pinned CSS file hashes and
checks literal `.html` selectors/states against **that project's release**, not
the CLI's candidate version. JSX/TSX/Vue/Svelte get **advisory literal
opening-tag checks**, including possible unknown class diagnostics, but these
files are **always reported as incomplete** because a full framework AST,
computed classes, and runtime behavior are not validated. Project-mode JSON
returns exit 0 on checked error-free HTML, 1 on errors, and 2 when coverage is
incomplete or there are no HTML files. Run framework-aware lint, tests and
browser accessibility checks separately.

`syntyr check` delegates to the existing static HTML validator when called
without `--project`.
It does not render templates, validate a running application or inspect
JavaScript/bundler imports. Its diagnostics return 1 for errors, 0 for
warnings-only or clean files, 2 for invalid inputs. Keep CSS and contract
versions matched. The optional `syntyr doctor` command additionally detects
literal duplicate/overlapping Syntyr CSS links and explicit mixed `/v/…/`
release pins, using the generated distribution ownership metadata. It
supports `--format json` and `--fail-on warning` for CI. It cannot infer
bundler-injected CSS or detect version drift in unversioned local filenames.

## Portable CLI ZIP

```sh
python3 scripts/package_cli.py /tmp/syntyr-cli.zip
unzip /tmp/syntyr-cli.zip
python3 syntyr-cli-0.3.0-alpha.5/scripts/syntyr_cli.py --help
```

The bundle includes the matching registry, Syntyr contract, version,
pinned published CSS, current source candidate CSS, portable Skill, and Python
scripts; it runs from any directory without a source checkout or internet access.
The build fails if committed registry JSON differs from its canonical generator,
or the validator contract version differs from `VERSION`.
The ZIP is a **source candidate**, not a published release.

All file writes must be reviewed in the dry-run plan. No automated cross-version
upgrades are supported; installations from a different version are rejected.

## Limits

This is a local advisory tool, not a browser runtime dependency, a secure
multi-user installation service, or a full HTML accessibility audit. Project
directories are assumed to be controlled by the invoking developer; do not
run the installer against directories being concurrently manipulated by
untrusted processes.
